Features Tiago Bravo vs. Samir Chantre and Joao Batista de Sousa vs. Nobuhiro Sawada in grappling bouts from London.
Features memorable matches from the Aces and Eights rise to the top, including Bully Ray vs. Jeff Hardy.
A look back at the storied IMPACT Wrestling career highs for "The Cowboy" James Storm, who has wrestled the most matches for the company in its 18 plus year history.
Lumbermen and settlers vie for an Idaho forest.
A man insists on taking a pipe organ to Utah.
Postal officials ask Harry, a gunman, to find a way to stop King Fisher from blocking mail from arriving in Uvalde; Fisher fears he will lose his power if he opens his road to the post office.
Robert Louis Stevenson is exploring a deserted mine with his son when they discover a Wells Fargo strongbox.
Lumberjack Will is attracted to Trudy, the daughter of his boss Mr. Bell; Trudy thinks highly of herself and Will refuses to indulge her spoiled, pampered ways.
A prospector's wife waits 22 years for a dress.
Jed is confronted with too many cooks and not enough vittles when he invites Pearl and Jethrine to Beverly Hills.
Trying to cool a feud between Granny and Pearl, Jed takes his family on a sightseeing tour of Beverly Hills.
Drysdale's marriage is threatened when he looks to the Clampetts for a housekeeper while his wife is away.
Two of Cousin Pearl's most ardent former suitors come to visit her in Beverly Hills; Jed doesn't know what to suggest.
Granny's plan to stop Pearl's yodeling backfires when the police she called find her illegal still.
Jed's bloodhound Duke takes on the role of matchmaker for his master and a glamorous woman from France.
A confidence man tries to sell Jed the Hollywood Bowl, Griffith Park and the Hollywood Freeway.
Jed is promoted to the position of bank vice president in order for him to participate in an interbank skeet shoot.
Cousin Pearl gets a glamour treatment and tries to groom the Clampetts for high society.
Jed takes a dose of Granny's tonic and ends up on Lovers Lane with a gold-digging secretary.
An IRS agent calls on the Clampetts and gets a roaring shotgun welcome from Granny.
Los Angeles Dodgers coach Leo Durocher finds a new pitcher in Jethro.
A Ponderosa ranch hand faces charges of killing the wife of the U.S. marshal who came to arrest him.
As Ben prepares to run for governor, Joe must come to his rescue when a disabled police officer from New Orleans comes to arrest Ben on a 20-year-old murder charge.
Adam is taken hostage by a band of U.S. Army prisoners who have escaped and sought refuge on the Ponderosa.
Two British socialites find that they still have a lot to learn when they visit their friends, the Cartwrights.
Shortly after the Ponderosa cattle herd arrives in San Francisco at the hands of Hoss, Joe and Ben, two of their trail drivers are shanghaied and destined for Hong Kong.
When a neighbor agrees to sell his property, the Cartwrights fear the loss of water rights for their cattle.
A man finds gold, then says he doesn't want it.
An outlaw-turned-lawman faces a moral dilemma.
A young cowpoke gets into a fight with a local over a girl and faces a harsh prison term.
Jack and Johnny left behind their outlaw ways and have a successful silver claim; Senator Stewart uses underhanded methods to obtain it and the men vow revenge.
Blue Feather pursues Bishop Lamy and Tom Forbes after his sister converts to Christianity; the bishop helps a man stricken with cholera, giving Tom a lesson on faith.
A girl sold into servitude goes to court.
A miner named Sawbuck saves a dentist from bandits and receives a set of gold crowns in return, but the dentist's attackers return to take Sawbuck's teeth.
Sheriff John Slaughter's deputy poses a problem; the maverick is prone to violence and accepting bribes.
Gold fever takes hold when Nellie learns that nuggets just lay on the ground in a remote area of Mexico.
A frontier couple battles Indians, outlaws and a government-issued land grant to save their ranch.

After several years away, FBI agent Henry Durand (Colin Hanks) returns to find his mother, Marty (Meg Ryan), a much different person: Having long mourned for Henry's father, she is now embracing single life. One day, while Marty, Henry and his new fiancée, Emily (Selma Blair), are out for a walk, they meet Tommy (Antonio Banderas), a mysterious stranger, with whom Marty then becomes involved. However, through his FBI contacts, Henry learns that Tommy is suspected of being an art thief.
Movie, Romantic comedy, Comedy, Crime drama, Romance

Veronica (Winona Ryder) is part of the most popular clique at her high school, but she disapproves of the other girls' cruel behavior. When Veronica and her new boyfriend, J.D. (Christian Slater), confront clique leader Heather Chandler (Kim Walker) and accidentally poison her, they make it appear a suicide. Soon Veronica realizes that J.D. is intentionally killing students he does not like. She races to stop J.D. while also clashing with the clique's new leader, Heather Duke (Shannen Doherty).
A middle-aged screenwriter (Kirstie Alley) enlists her young nephew (Eric Christian Olsen) to pass himself off as the author of her scripts.

Marijuana growers Jack (Billy Bob Thornton), Carter (Hank Azaria) and Harlan (Ryan Phillippe) are looking at a big payoff for their crop -- until head honcho Malcolm (John Lithgow) is murdered. Wanting a bigger piece of the proverbial pie, the three men decide to keep Malcolm's demise a secret, selling the stash themselves and pocketing all the profits. But, when they get involved with some very dangerous characters in the drug industry, the men start to question the wisdom of their scheme.
Ironic buyers have a hot new card; how to spot suspicious Halloween candy; who splits the check?
How to pick up girls without words; are apples attractive?; "Die Hard" gets rejected by executives.
"Jurassic Park" gets rejected by executives; how a Wonder of the World came to be.

The Wanted gets some unwanted advice; a visit to the psych ward; Moshe Kasher's future.
Jessica Lowe on texting; commentary on a bar fight; can you date your friend's ex?
Danny Krissler's acting reel; what if there was a zombie movie with real zombies?; Check, please.
Belle and Bernice have a career in fashion; cabinet raids at a '90s sleepover; Jon Glaser is in heaven.
A paranormal investigation; something seems fishy; Alec Baldwin talks to Taylor and Cody.
Celebrating Scott's 100th portrayal of a waiter; Hecubus is fired and rehired; a wife walks in on her husband and a thief in bed.
The Bearded Lady; spy models; a horny patient.
Skits include: "Chicken Lady at a Strip Bar," "Queen Speaks to Canada" and "Bar Fight."
The feathers go flying when the Chicken Lady spots Rooster Boy; Cabbie has his own set of road rules; some cops have more important things to discuss than a dead body.
Puppy won't do tricks; a man who dresses his best to get the paper; a sleepwalking boy steals his dad's money; a restaurant that has a relationship section.
A construction worker firmly denies sleeping on the job; Bruce discovers that he is only 17 inches tall.
A magical flying pig; the Best Actor award at the Oscars results; an axe murderer politely asks an old lady if he can borrow her axe; men wear earrings in the '90s.
A new church member makes Umma feel cast aside; Appa becomes jealous of Janet's journaling; Shannon's decision to allow shorts in the office allows Terence to come out of his shell.
Appa destroys a piece of Gerald's childhood; Umma misrepresents herself to her support group; Shannon gets in the way of Kimchee's plan to visit Jung in California.
Umma and Appa try to fit in at an upscale tennis court; Shannon helps Omar deal with his over-eager family; Janet misjudges a co-worker.
Appa finds marijuana in the house; Shannon throws a staff party that doesn't go as planned.
Appa and Kimchee enjoy an impromptu hangout together; Janet and Umma find an envelope of money in the store; Jung and Shannon struggle to watch TV together.
Appa worries about Umma after a minor household accident; Janet uses Jung's past to boost her reputation with students; a high school reunion has Kimchee thinking about an old flame.
Appa makes a controversial call when umpiring pastor Nina's baseball game; Janet gives Umma a sweater that turns out to be a bad fit; Jung and Kimchee babysit Gwen's niece.
Air-headed arsonist; crook leaves shoe behind; burglar gets stuck in a window.
Shoplifter hides a mink coat in her pants; police give drunks with a sawed-off shotgun directions to jail; witness throws a toilet at a criminal.
A bank robber uses his phone bill to light a fuse; incontinent burglar; parents ask for marijuana used as evidence in their son's trial.
Marijuana farmer tries to claim his confiscated crop; robber battles change machine; shoplifter tries to sell merchandise.
A dog leads cops to its pot possessing owners; a new tool for law enforcement; a thief gets a flood of trouble.
Criminals try to enter a house through the chimney; cab driver; a man who should have called for a ride.
A clumsy crook is arrested for stepping on a woman; drunken motorist claims he's a "devastated driver."
A criminal misses his exit; a criminal-tagging pizza; misguided men make a wrong turn.
A boy (Julian Dennison) and his foster father (Sam Neill) become the subjects of a manhunt after they get stranded in the New Zealand wilderness.

El reto consiste en cocinar con lo básico, al vapor, hervido o escalfado, cada participante debe preparar una proteína y hacer un platillo espectacular. En el servicio de este capítulo servirán sashimi en la mesa.
Los restantes 12 concursantes compiten en un desafío intenso y enfrentan la eliminación.
Llegan Hallie y Christina y marcan el reto: cocinar con cerveza. Cada participante debe crear un platillo con uno o más tipos de cerveza.

Gordon Ramsay les pide nominar a alguien para ser su líder, y para el equipo azul es un proceso rápido, pero para el rojo es un gran problema. El chef Ramsay sorprende a los competidores al pedirles reinterpretar 5 clásicos de comida estadounidense.

Los concursantes tienen el reto de preparar postres para una cena romántica. El equipo ganador se lleva un viaje de lujo a Las Vegas, mientras que los perdedores deben realizar los preparativos para la cena de la próxima "noche de cita".
El Meiji Kinenkan es el salón nupcial más antiguo de Japón que se está reformando para celebrar su 50.º aniversario, lo que incluye la incorporación de un restaurante chino y su nuevo gran chef.
Iron Chef Chen hace su mejor presentación de yogur contra el retador Junichi Ito, conocido como el científico de la cocina.
El Iron Chef Morimoto se enfrenta a su contrincante Tsuyoshi Kajimoto para innovar con el abulón, un marisco.

Iron Chef es llamado a enfrentarse a Miyoko Sakai, una afamada crítica gastronómica tailandesa que ha tenido el privilegio de conocer los secretos de la cocina real tailandesa directamente de la fuente.
El retador en esta batalla del melocotón es Masanobu Watabe, propietario de Le Rameau d'Or en Yokohama, Japón. Watabe dirige él solo el restaurante para 22 clientes.
El contrincante de Chen es un hombre que domina la cocina china de estilo chaozhou, un estilo exigente que realmente es capaz de complacer los sensibles gustos de los clientes de Kioto.

Sakai se enfrenta al "prestidigitador del ajo", un chef que abraza este ingrediente picante como lo hacen los verdaderos italianos; Sakai se enfrenta además al reto de utilizar calamares vivos en los platos.
Tres años después de perder ante el Iron Chef Chen, el restaurante italiano Sabatini pide la revancha, esta vez enviando al maestro de cocina de su restaurante de Tokio.
En honor al Festival de las Niñas, Kaga invita a un retador de la antigua ciudad de Kamakura, Motohito Kondo, que se formó en Kioto y es un experto tanto en té como en sake.
Tasaki es un campeón mundial de sumillería que siempre ha soñado con convertirse en un afamado chef; el presidente Kaga decide concederle su deseo.
Después de que dos de sus hombres perdieran ante Chen, el gran chef de Heichinrou decide que él será el próximo oponente para que pueda recuperar el orgullo del amado restaurante.
El Chef Ramsay hace que los concursantes creen un solo bocadillo para crear una audaz primera impresión; los equipos muestran una falta de cooperación durante la cena.
Un nuevo reto para los chefs, tienen que preparar un desayuno gourmet en un food truck de última generación para ochenta personas. El ganador tiene un cambio de estilo y vestuario.
Los chefs tendrán que preparar un platillo fusión de dos cocinas de diferentes países, un gran reto y sorpresas se llevan con el resultado. Se acerca la final y solo dos chefs llegan hasta el último.

Los dos concursantes finalistas deben crear una comida de 5 platos para ser juzgados por personajes distinguidos en la comunidad de comida de Los Ángeles; invitados especiales asisten al servicio de cena; el ganador es elegido.
Ramsay ayuda a un restaurante en Sherman Oaks, California, donde las peleas entre hermanos Alex y Celine son constantes.
Ramsay ayuda a los dueños gemelos de un restaurante italiano en Eagle Rock, California.
Ayudando a un restaurante en dificultades en Pasadena, California.
Ramsay viaja a Nueva Orleans para mejorar un restaurante cuya calidad se ha venido a menos debido a su decoración y menú desastroso.
El chef Ramsay visita restaurantes a los que ayudó en el pasado (Lido, Anna Vincenzo, Le Bistro) para comprobar cómo han evolucionado y si han seguido sus consejos.
Gordon intenta ayudar a devolver al éxito a un abandonado restaurante de California. El chef Ramsay causa revuelo cuando sugiere cambiar la decoración fea, el menú y la cocina sucia.

Gordon intenta mejorar los negocios en un elegante restaurante de California que necesita clientela desesperadamente. El chef ejecutivo tiene un enfrentamiento con Gordon frente a todo el equipo de trabajo.
El Iron Chef Kobe se enfrenta a un chef de cocina italiana inusual que opera desde su propio carrito de comida.
A disrespected but decent British detective unravels a cold case about a missing seventeen-year-old girl while trying to deal with the breakup of his marriage.
The death of a local farmer leads Blake to Ballarat's murky world of late night backstreet gambling and two feuding brothers with contrasting fortunes.
A young woman is shot dead at a bonfire night celebration; the police immediately arrest an aboriginal boy she knew for her murder.
Tensions flare up between local workers and some communist students.
A famous actress comes to the Colonists Club and stuns everyone by dropping dead onstage.
Frost suspects that a young soldier killed on maneuvers was murdered.
After finishing a rowing race, a winning team member dies after being thrown into Lake Wendouree during celebrations.
War throws Florence into chaos, and Piero, Cosimo's only son, is anxious to join the fight, but Lucrezia, the boy's mother, tries to prevent him from going.
The family hopes for refuge in the countryside from the contagion, but Marco remains in Florence.
In front of the Signoria, Albizzi accuses Cosimo of plotting to become the city dictator.
Circumstances continue to go downhill in Florence while the family remains in exile; Albizzi takes control of Florence.

Gina is a beautiful young woman who's still haunted by the accident that took her sight years earlier. Living in Bangkok with her husband, James, she undergoes a cutting-edge operation that restores the vision to her right eye. Now that Gina can see again, she slowly starts to realize that her newfound independence makes James feel jealous, threatened and insecure.
Emma is surprised to learn the donor of her new heart was her estranged cousin, but the bigger secret is that the girl was murdered -- and maybe by someone Emma knows very well.

On their way home from China, married Christian missionaries Roy (Woody Harrelson) and Jessie (Emily Mortimer) take a train from Beijing to Moscow. On board, they befriend Carlos (Eduardo Noriega) and Abby (Kate Mara). When Roy does not return in time at one stop, Jessie waits for him to catch up at the next station. Carlos and Abby stay with her, insisting the town is unsafe, however Carlos' attempts to "befriend" Jessie radically change the dynamic of the trip.
John Watkins, Canada's ambassador to Moscow, is suspected of being a communist spy. Based on a true story.

Megan moves across the country to rebuild her life. When she runs into one of her former colleagues, she is pleasantly surprised and the pair become close friends. When he wants more from her, he begins sabotaging everything in Megan's life.

Carter receives a collect call from Vinnie, and a dark event from the past threatens to destroy his current success. Once a good friend of Carter's, Vinnie is now a deluded barfly living in a small town in California. He has gotten himself into trouble and calls Carter to bail him out before the truth about their past - their involvement in a horse racing scam which resulted in the ruin of an innocent man - comes to light.
A mounted fish moves, household objects levitate, and monsters haunt a troubled novelist (William Katt).
Four friends travel into the Australian Outback to see Charlie's Farm, the site where a family met a gruesome end.
Members (Charisma Carpenter, Corin Nemec) of a reality TV show investigate a supposedly haunted house.
A herpetologist helps a detective track her flushed-away pet, now a king-size mutant called Ramone.
Becoming paranoid after his research into serial killers, a writer (Simon Pegg) must confront his numerous demons in order to make it to an important meeting about his screenplay.

Cop Katie Sullivan (Gretchen Becker) shoots two crooks who are robbing a store, and though she's also wounded in the process, reporters cast her as a trigger-happy rogue. Devious police department bosses, hoping to get rid of a public relations problem, plan to kill Sullivan. But Matt Cordell (Robert Z'Dar), a dead cop who's just been resurrected, takes a liking to Sullivan and is determined to mow down her enemies before a police detective, Sean McKinney (Robert Davi), can stop him.
On a trip to Colombia, a group of college students encounter a sixty-foot boa constrictor, hungry for blood.
After noticing her swamp nest is missing an egg, an angry crocodile stalks college students (Mark McLachlan, Caitlin Martin, Chris Solari) on a houseboat for spring break.
A wild animal goes on a bloodthirsty rampage on the Appalachian Trail.

Peter (John Hargreaves) and Marcia (Briony Behets), a bitter married couple teetering on the edge of divorce, take a camping trip to heal the rift between them. As the weekend progresses, the selfish pair engage in reckless behavior that demonstrates an increasing disrespect for their natural surroundings. When Peter and Marcia become the targets of a series of inexplicable animal attacks, it becomes clear that an angry Mother Nature has come to exact her revenge.

Unseen forces attack the passengers and crew on an international flight. As the people fight to stay alive, they realize that the unseen forces are the spirits of murdered girls. The spirits try to stop their killer, who is onboard the plane.
A giant octopus, mutated from years of radiation exposure, attacks a Navy submarine transporting a terrorist (Ravil Isyanov) captured by a CIA agent (Jay Harrington).

Alexandra (Stephanie Niznik) and Jason (Greg Cromer) are a married couple whose yacht fails to withstand a storm at sea. They're saved from the stormy waters by Capt. Bigelow (Daniel Quinn) and his crew, who man a cargo ship. Jason is heavily drugged by the ship's doctor, Gerbac (Richard Moll), and realizes something is amiss when he comes across corpses. Meanwhile, Gerbac is working on a dangerous scientific experiment using spider eggs, which he hopes to implant in Jason's body.
Sailors go to sea to hunt for a prehistoric shark, previously thought to be extinct.
Spurned by a Marilyn Monroe look-alike (Linda Kerridge), a film buff (Dennis Christopher) becomes a killer costumed as classic screen characters.
Barnaby y Winter usan un cómic para encontrar al asesino de una ex-supermodelo durante el festival de cómics de Carver Valley.
Barnaby y Winter sacan a relucir viejos rencores, asuntos íntimos y chocolates artesanales para encontrar al culpable de una muerte en un club de rugby.
Durante una reunión de antiguos alumnos de la escuela secundaria, Sídney vuelve a encontrarse con su exnovio, Tony. Él quiere ir con Sídney a Hawái para que lo ayude a buscar el Ídolo de Lono.
El padre de Sídney, un constructor de presas, la envía a China para recuperar una estatua sagrada de un grupo de monjes que rechazan abandonar el territorio de los Tres Ríos.
Sydney, Nigel y el millonario Rod Thorson viajan a la selva para hallar a un equipo de Buscadores de Reliquias que desapareció mientras buscaba el artefacto más antiguo del mundo.
Dos estudiantes graduados desaparecen mientras buscan la Cruz de Utu haitiana que supuestamente posee poderes increíbles.
Sydney y Nigel intentan salvar a una Buscadora de Reliquias novata de perder su cabeza mientras busca una mítica pechera de César.
Sídney y Nigel descubren lo que aparentan ser unos artefactos egipcios sin descubrir en un estudio de cine en Londres.
Claudia asegura haber conocido a Cleopatra en su vida anterior y es investigada cuando ella revela un compartimiento secreto en el joyero de la reina egipcia.
Después de una emboscada, Sídney es capturada por un cazador. Nigel y Claudia se enfrentan a cazadores rivales que quieren vender los tesoros por dinero.
Sydney es secuestrada y Cate, Nigel y Claudia tienen que determinar cuál de sus enemigos la ha raptado.
A pesar de los rumores que hablan de la existencia de hombres lobo, Sydney y Nigel van hacia los Cárpatos en busca del Halcón de Oro de Mirabor.
Sídney se convierte en parte de una de las profecías de Nostradamus cuando ella tiene que evitar que un asesino mate a un miembro de la familia real.

Un viejo amigo que trabaja en el Museo del Louvre, en París, le pide a Sídney que le ayude a buscar el cetro de rubíes que perteneció al legendario rey germano Günther el Valiente, antes de que los ladrones consigan sacarlo del país.
Martin debe tratar a un anciano con un olor horrible. Un presentador de radio local parece tener un problema con la bebida. Julie Mitchell llega a Portwenn.
Culpan a Martín cuando un paciente muere durante un examen. Joan insta a Martín a explicar al viudo las circunstancias que rodean la muerte de Helen.
Martín se ve sorprendido y desconcertado cuando sus padres llegan repentinamente de visita. El examen de Martín a una mujer conduce a un diagnóstico sorpresa.
Tennison investiga la muerte del gerente del exclusivo Club Huntington.
Tennison es apartada de un caso y se rumorea que podría ser reemplazada. Mientras tanto, la esposa de Marlow es interrogada.
La presencia de Barnaby en la boda de la amiga de Sarah resulta fatídica cuando un asesino tiene como objetivo a las novias locales y conduce al detective a una misión para atrapar al asesino.
Barnaby debe enfrentarse a sus miedos luego de que los avistamientos de payasos, notas siniestras y la muerte acompañaron a Ferraees Circo a la ciudad.
Los dos finalistas compiten por el puesto de jefe de cocina en BLT Steak en Nueva York.

John Wayne Gacy murdered 33 boys and young men during a six-year period in the 1970s; he was well-liked in the community he lived in and would often dress up for kids' parties, earning himself the nickname Killer Clown.
A look at the Welsh serial killer known to some as The Wildman, who got four life sentences for a string of gruesome murders and sexual assaults.
From 1975 to 1980, Billy Mansfield Jr murdered at least five victims in California and Florida; investigators suspect that the serial killer may have taken more lives.
A cult killer portrays himself as a pillar of the community, but the story is more sinister.
When Tia Sharp disappears, Stuart Hazell helps police search for her, but in reality he had murdered the 12-year-old.
When a businessman vanishes, police are led to Pamela Moss, an unassuming woman with terrifying secrets.
Natalie Bennett embarks on years of coercively controlling her boyfriend before ending his life with murder.
Following a Texas man's sudden diabetic coma, the crimes of his wife Sarah Hartsfield are exposed.

Musician and special needs teacher Jane Longhurst vanishes during her day off work after making a plan to go swimming with her friend's boyfriend; five weeks later, Jane's partially decomposed body is found burning 25 miles from Jane's home.
Pawel Relowicz rapes and kills 21-year-old Hull student Libby Squire in a case that made headlines around the UK.

In Florida, a 13-year-old girl is found stabbed over a hundred times; a teenager with a knife obsession comes under suspicion; in Colorado, a woman picked up in a creepy white van after a night out is missing.

In the U.K., a young woman fails to come home after a mysterious date; her worried family desperately searches for her, only to discover a devious attempt at a cover-up; in the U.S., a young mother is found dead in a house fire.
Surveillance footage plays a central role in tracking down the killers in two murder cases.
Convicted killer Glyn Dix told his new wife Hazel he was the victim of a miscarriage of justice, then, he struck again.
Claire and Andrew Tavener were a sociable couple; when Andrew got drunk, he became paranoid and violent.
Assia Newton had left her abusive marriage and dreamt of a new life with her Tunisian lover, but her estranged husband had other plans.
When Arlene Fraser disappeared, her husband Nat had a watertight alibi; local cops weren't fooled.
Nick Groff spends two days in Hallettsville, Texas' haunted location called the "Old Lavaca Jail."

Nick spends forty-eight hours inside a haunted clinic using new equipment to see if he can communicate with the entities that seem to be going out of their way to scare and sometimes physically lash out at the living.

Nick Groff conducts a paranormal investigation and tries to make physical contact with the deceased patients of the hospital using a new piece of paranormal equipment that utilizes motion detecting lasers.

Nick will investigate this partially vacant, square foot building throughout the day and night and see if he can document any paranormal activity and find out if something here will reveal the secrets of what occurred behind these walls that have long been shrouded in secrecy for so many years.
Whilst being transported on a bus, Ricky Dubose killed two correctional officers before going on the run.
Born into a notorious crime family, robber-turned-killer Erica Jenkins goes on a murder spree in Omaha.
Remorseless murderer Casey Pigge's main ambition is to be the ultimate serial killer.
A fake dating profile leads Michael Sandy into deadly danger.
A teenager's online romance ends in tragedy.
A marshal from another territory comes to North Fork looking for a wanted man.
An escaped killer barricades himself and his two companions in the North Fork general store.
Mark meets a stranger whom Lucas suspects of being a wanted man.
A young man wants an education despite his uncle's objection.
The young son of a neighboring rancher is seriously hurt in an accident.
The North Fork schoolteacher is pressured to leave town because of her progressive ideas.
A hired gunman arrives in town to kill a man Lucas has hated for years.
Lucas gives his blood to save a dying man.
Mark's finding of the body of a murder victim starts Lucas, his friend Artemus and Marshal Torrance on a search for the killer.
A band of Indians kidnaps Mark and disappears into the hills.

Lucas is the town's representative to the railroad commission until an infamous train robber dies and leaves his ill-gotten wealth to Lucas; Lucas must clear his name and stop the reckless ambition of his replacement.
When a rancher dies after the bank forecloses the mortgage on his property, his son blames the banker for his father's death.
A rancher is shot by an unknown killer, and his daughter's lover is jailed.
A group of outlaws devises a plan to get rid of Lucas so that they can take over the town of North Fork.
After Lucas kills a mountain man in a barroom brawl, his father arrives in North Fork determined to take revenge on Lucas and Marshal Torrance, once he breaks his other two boys out of jail.
A dying gunslinger attracts trouble to North Fork.
Lucas and Mark lie to protect a dead man's family.
Lucas becomes involved in the family troubles of the hotel clerk.
Fallen ill, a couple seeks shelter with Lucas.
Lucas and Mark travel across the desert, returning from a trip to lay in a supply of salt.
Lucas agrees to ride shotgun on the North Fork stage.
Outlaws threaten to kill Micah unless their leader is freed.
The town drunk's son thinks he is heir to Lucas' ranch.
Lucas and Mark find themselves caring for a 6-month-old baby.
Lucas becomes involved in a revenge fight when he befriends a young Easterner.
A buffalo hunter tries to force Lucas into a gunfight.
Land-hungry brothers threaten a spinster's fiancé.
Two tough private detectives appear in North Fork looking for a boy.
Two unhappy heirs threaten a young widow.
A boy is accused of shooting an outlaw in the back.
When a horse dealer transporting a prize stallion stops in North Fork, two saddle tramps try to use trickery to obtain it.
An elderly couple moves to North Fork under an assumed name to hide the fact that they are the parents of a vicious killer; the plan backfires when the son shows up at their home.
After foiling a girl's attempt to rob the general store, Lucas finds that she and her brother are plotting the murder of their abusive stepfather.
Newspaperman Byron Claremont specializes in profiles of gunmen; one of his stories is responsible for an old-time marshal's death; and his next subject is Lucas.

The unthinkable happens when heavily armed and highly trained terrorists launch a bold daytime attack on the White House. The building is overrun, and President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart) and his staff are taken hostage. Luckily for Asher, former presidential security officer Mike Banning (Gerard Butler) is on the scene. With time running out, it's up to Banning to locate Asher's son before the extremists do and rescue the president before his captors unleash their ultimate plan.

After the death of the British prime minister, the world's most powerful leaders gather in London to pay their respects. Without warning, terrorists unleash a devastating attack that leaves the city in chaos and ruins. Secret Service agent Mike Banning (Gerard Butler) springs into action to bring U.S. President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart) to safety. When Asher falls into the hands of the sinister organization, it's up to Banning to save his commander in chief from a horrible fate.

Andy (Philip Seymour Hoffman), a debt-ridden broker, needs some quick cash. He ropes his younger brother, Hank (Ethan Hawke), into a scheme to commit the perfect crime: to rob their parents' (Albert Finney, Rosemary Harris) jewelry store. The scheme goes horribly awry, and the family patriarch takes justice into his own hands, unaware that the criminals he is hunting are his own sons.

Young couple Malcolm (Marlon Wayans) and Kisha (Essence Atkins) have just moved into their dream home. As they settle in, they learn that they're not alone -- not because the house is haunted, but because Kisha is possessed by a demon. Desperate to salvage his relationship -- and more importantly -- his sex life -- Malcolm hires a coterie of paranormal specialists, which includes a priest and ghostbusters, to banish the unwelcome intruder from Kisha's body.

After the ordeal he suffered with his now former girlfriend's (Essence Atkins) demonic possession, Malcolm (Marlon Wayans) has decided to start fresh. He has a new girlfriend named Megan (Jaime Pressly), and they and Megan's children are moving into their dream home. Soon afterward, Malcolm is once again plagued by supernatural shenanigans -- only this time, it's not just the house that's haunted. A demon has attached itself to Malcolm, and shows no signs of letting go.

His faith broken by many years fighting in the Crusades, a knight named Behman returns to Europe and finds it ravaged by the Black Plague. A dying cardinal orders Behman and his friend, Felson, to take an accused witch to a remote abbey, where monks will destroy her powers and end the pestilence. As Behman and five comrades undertake the dangerous journey, they come to realize that the prisoner is no ordinary girl, and evil forces await at the destination.
A former college athlete (Matthew McConaughey) joins forces with a sports consultant (Al Pacino) to handicap football games for high-rolling gamblers.

Longtime LAPD partners and friends, Brian Taylor (Jake Gyllenhaal) and Mike Zavala (Michael Peña) patrol one of the most dangerous neighborhoods in Los Angeles. Though they may bend the rules, their honor and dedication to the job are unquestioned. Taylor and Zavala always have each other's back, even if Taylor's surreptitious filming of their daily activities for a college course is a bit ill-advised. All hell breaks loose for the officers when they run afoul of a vicious Mexican cartel.

After a string of bizarre bank robberies in Southern California, with the crooks donning masks of various former presidents, a federal agent, Johnny Utah (Keanu Reeves), infiltrates the suspected gang. But this is no ordinary group of robbers. They're surfers -- led by the charismatic Bodhi (Patrick Swayze) -- who are addicted to the rush of thievery. But when Utah falls in love with a female surfer, Tyler (Lori Petty), who is close to the gang, it complicates his sense of duty.
Walker investigates encounters with UFOs in a small Texas town and tries to prove the residents have been deceived for the past 40 years.
Walker time-travels to the 1860s to trace the disappearance of gold and the murder of a legendary ranger.
Walker time-travels to the 1860s to trace the disappearance of gold and the murder of a legendary ranger.

Dr. Ben Song, lead physicist of a top-secret government time-travel program known as Quantum Leap, makes an unauthorized leap into the past, awakening in a different body with only fragments of his memory intact. Guided by Addison, a colleague in the present day who appears to him as a hologram that only he can see and hear, he discovers the only way for him to leap again is to correct something in his host person's life. As Ben leaps from life to life, putting right what once went wrong, his team in the present tries to figure out why he leaped and bring him home.

Reno discovers that a racketeer he is tracking is also wanted by a crime boss for stealing his girlfriend.
Reno becomes a hostage in a small-town saloon when he takes refuge from a storm; Bobby struggles to come to terms with the way he lives.

Game show series have been making a comeback in television, and media and "America Says" is no exception. This program is following in the footsteps of the popular mobile app game "HQ Trivia." The network is planning its own spin on the game show, and Fran Shea, evp, programming and marketing, says she "has been studying the GSN audience and prepared a slate of new shows that reflect what it wants: family-friendly, fun, escapist television." In "America Says," two teams face off to guess Americans' responses to questions covering a variety of topics. Michael Higgins is the host.
Joey Fatone hosts as teams compete to answer practical, everyday questions, such as which lane has the smoothest flow of traffic on the highway.
Teams of three compete to answer practical, everyday questions that everyone should know, such as what you should do to your outdoor plants to protect them from frost.
An old flame of Jonathan's (Christine Belford) seems unwilling to go through with her wedding in Monte Carlo.
A gold statue of Buddha leads to a world of Asian intrigue and pursuing gangsters; guest Edward Mulhare.
Jennifer plans to surprise Jonathan with her portrait, until the artist is found slain.
Florida is asked to be the television spokeswoman for a new health tonic.
The family tries to convince James that he should see a doctor for his headaches and emotional outbursts.
The most popular girl in high school turns J.J. into a one-woman man.
Florida promises to burst into a full-fledged hurricane unless someone can figure out what triggered the storm.
After a doctor fails to find the reason for his headache, Lamont consults a psychiatrist to treat his pain.
Fred asks a professional gambler to teach Lamont and his friends a lesson.
When Lamont falls for an older woman, Fred schemes to show him how ridiculous it is.
Lamont and Rollo mistakenly think Fred has only six months to live and set him up on a date with Lena Horne.
When teenage cadets appear to have brutalized five homosexual men, Hanson and Penhall investigate at a tough military academy.
After a teen idol receives death threats, Hanson and Penhall provide protection on the set of the young actor's latest project.

Detective Sgt. Rick Hunter fights crime in the San Diego area. The wily homicide investigator isn't afraid to break the rules as he pursues justice, though the perpetrators he and his partners are after frequently end up dead. Criticized for its graphic violence, the show also features witty banter between Hunter and his partner.
Rick and Dee Dee's investigation of an actress's mysterious demise uncovers a sister very eager to collect the inheritance.

Jim Rockford is an ex-con and private detective. He was falsely convicted of a crime he didn't commit, but that doesn't stop him from using his ex-con buddies to help him solve crimes. Nothing comes easy for Rockford, but he works hard and usually gets shot at or beat up at least once per episode.
Walker and Trivette protect a Mexican presidential candidate from an international assassin hired by an imprisoned drug-lord.
Chico Kwasi faces Teodor Hristov for the GLORY Welterweight World Championship at RTM Stage Rotterdam in Rotterdam, Netherlands.
From Dec. 10, 2016. Features Tiffany van Soest vs. Jessica Gladstone, Danyo Ilunga vs. Michael Duut and Harut Grigorian vs. Danijel Solaja from Oberhausen, Germany.
Sittichai Sitsongpeenong vs. Marat Grigorian for the GLORY lightweight title, plus a one-night, single-elimination lightweight contender tournament. From Dec. 10. 2016 in Oberhausen, Germany.
Rico Verhoeven defends his title against Jamal Ben Saddik along with three additional fights from the GelreDome in Arnhem, Netherlands.
Brazilian GLORY middleweight champion Alex "Po Atan" Pereira headlines, putting his title on the line against Ertugrul Bayrak in a main event fight set for five rounds.

With base camp set up and the cold setting in, Chris and Casey must find food fast.
Mentally drained and hungry, the brothers must try new tactics to find food and warmth.

A Michigan conservation officer looks into an illegal deer during firearm deer season; the state's DNR offers tips on how to bag a bear, and conservation officer recruits receive lessons in operating snowmobiles.
A Michigan conservation officer in the state's Upper Peninsula checks on waterfowl hunters and looks into a case of discarded deer carcasses.
D-3 Officers check on hunters in the northern Lower Peninsula.
Walleye fishing in the southern part of the state and the northern part, in the spring and through the ice as well as a look at Michigan's DNR partnering with the National Guard.

Full-auto airguns shooting firebirds as fast as possible in a head-to-head challenge.
Sunrise gives life to the valley and animals are on the move.
Chris and Casey Keefer are back in the Saskatchewan bushland to test their survival skills.

One of the most sought after wilderness destinations in the world, the Okavango Delta in Botswana is what dreams are made of - the heart-stopping excitement of big game viewing, the supreme tranquility and serenity of an untouched delta.

The Pongola River descends steeply from the Lebombo Mountain range in KwaZulu-Natal below Lake Jozini. Here the river meanders to the Pongola Floodplain. But a secret lies at the bottom of South Africa's largest and most diverse freshwater ecosystem!
Bloemhof Dam lies deep in the cultural Heartland of South Africa's North West Province, with a multitude of fresh water fish on offer; this is a species hunt that you will not want to miss.

Craig is hunting down the ultimate estuarine predator, the elusive River Snapper. The protected waters of the St Lucia section of the Isimangaliso Wetland Park is a renowned destination for this dirty fighter but it will take all of Craig's cunning.

There's only one way to really cover a large section of the Indian Ocean and that's in the comforts of a live-aboard yacht; Tommo sails to Northern Mozambique, looking for new coral reefs and any nervous water that would provide entertainment.

The warm currents of the Indian Ocean provide a bounty of species for anglers to target. Join Tommo and Wes as they cruise around the islands off Vilanculos hunting for the resident fish for which these reefs are renowned.

The Kruger Park is as wild as any natural environment can get. Gareth and Tommo get invited by the scientific services to take part in research of the Sabie River, their survey samples waters that have never been fished before.

African rivers are home to many dangerous animals, none more so than the man-eating Nile Crocodile. In our pursuit of trophy tigers, we learn firsthand how quickly this wily and ancient beast can turn the tables.

The Autumn and Spring seasons remain the favorite window in which to tackle the wild Brown Trout of the Natal Midlands in South Africa, largely due to their temperament at this time of year, but also because the weather conditions and water...

Majestic Mount Kenya rises to over 5000 meters and this magnificent monolithic often shrouded by mist and snow, hard to believe this close to the equator. But the pristine streams running down the valleys hold plump Trout ready and willing to snap...

When we heard word of aquatic research taking place in South Africa's largest game reserve, the Kruger National Park, a real opportunity to encounter fish in a wild habitat, that had not yet seen a fly, was immediately seized upon.

The estuaries of Angola are the nursery for all fish that roam off its cold Atlantic seaboard, and it's where in certain seasons the Jacks and Tarpon are to be found. Tommo and Wes split up to experiment in two of Angola's most prolific waterways.
Laramy Miller explores new territory in the western plateaus of Texas; this loud, open country is a challenge; but Laramy proves that with the right amount of patience, he can stalk in on anything.
Laramie must act quickly, before the coyotes scare the elk herds out of these mountains.
With only his old black powder gun for protection, Laramy needs to make sure that he sees the bear before the bear spots him.
Laramy has a vast number of mule deer to choose from in West Texas.
In search of elk, Laramy has made the long journey on horseback deep into these Montana Mountains.

Laramy shows his trapping skills as he traps for all sorts of critters near his mountain home.
Laramy thinks back over his favorite hunts throughout the series, and gives a heartfelt farewell.

Nathan Ratchford goes back in time to the old hunting camps of the Maine Northwoods after Ruffed Grouse; an iconic species in an iconic place, with a flushing lab and endless acres of forest to pursue them.

Monty Don turns his attention to planting out his sweet peas and potting up lilies, and Carol Klein returns to Gloucestershire to help first-time gardeners, Dan and Dominique, plant up their new border in the style of a cottage garden.

With autumn just around the corner, Adam takes stock of his garden and plans ahead for some late-season interest under the supervision of Ash the cat. Plus, Frances visits a garden in Kent where the plants provide a non-stop buffet for insects.

The vegetable garden is at its peak now and as well as harvesting, Monty has a look at how his autumn crops are faring as well as giving tips on how to keep the garden looking at its best. Adam Frost returns to Leicester where he has been helping to create a garden from scratch on a new build estate, and Frances Tophill celebrates the summer harvest on her shared allotment.
Monty and the team celebrate the wonder of trees and explore the vital role they play in gardens and the wider landscape. Zoe Ball joins Toby Buckland on a visit to a tree project in North London.

Join Adam in his garden for a seasonal catch-up. Toby Buckland gives timely tips on summer and autumn maintenance for borders, plus join singer-songwriter Billie Marten as she shares her passion for growing vegetables.

Monty gives tips on moving plants which are in the wrong place or have outgrown their space, shows how to store chillies and harvests the last of his tomatoes. Rachel de Thame returns to Longmeadow to talk to Monty about her return to health and to plant up pots for spring colour.

Monty Don harvests apples, pears and quince and plants indoor bulbs, we meet a Northern Irish daffodil breeder, and Carol Klein travels to Wales to explore the Eupatorium with a passionate gardener who has a rare and spectacular collection.

After an extraordinary season, Monty's orchard has a bountiful harvest of apples and he gives advice on how to pick and store them. Frances Tophill makes a final visit to her shared allotment and joins in with the festivities at their annual show. Adam Frost visits the RHS garden Wisley where he meets the Curator to discuss the effects of summer. Nick Bailey investigates knotweed, one of the most pernicious weeds in the UK, Arit Anderson provides inspiration for colourful late season containers.
Monty Don prepares for his spring display and tackles slippery paths, Carol Klein visits a collection of Michaelmas daisies, and we visit a veg grower with a show-stopping Halloween pumpkin.

At Longmeadow, Monty shows how to harvest and store potatoes. He also adds late summer colour to the cottage garden and prunes shrub roses. Carol Klein travels to Norfolk to meet Adrian Bloom, a member of a horticultural dynasty.

Monty propagates succulent plants, revisits his container vegetable garden, and gives advice on how to get a good crop of pumpkins. Adam looks a new garden at RHS Hyde Hall in Essex, and Rachel visits a garden of vibrant colours in Wiltshire.

A celebration of people who are growing their own, from vegetables to flowers, across the UK. At Longmeadow, Monty shares tips and advice on how to get the most out of bargain plants. Meanwhile, Joe visits an extraordinary food project in Bristol.

Monty Don tackles the perennial problem of what to grow in the shade beneath a tree, Carol Klein has a look at the crocosmia, and we meet a gardener in Derbyshire who has spent a lifetime growing and showing gladioli.

Monty plants for pollinators in the Wildlife Garden and trims his box topiary cones. He also takes succulent leaf cuttings and continues the summer veg harvest. Meanwhile, Carol Klein visits stunning Italian-influenced gardens in Gloucestershire.
Monty Don tackles some seasonal gardening jobs at Longmeadow and guest presenter Matthew Wilson has some ideas to brighten up a dark, north-facing wall.
As autumn unfolds in the garden, Monty Don and Nigel make the most of the season and prepare for the winter ahead. Meanwhile, Carol Klein is in Surrey looking at wild and cultivated heathers.
Monty gives more advice on tomato-growing, Nick Bailey travels to South Africa in search of the cousins of the Crocosmia, and Advolly Richmond looks at the Victorian trend of garden theme parks.
As the plants in the jewel garden reach the peak of their late summer glory, Monty starts planning for the spring when he plants ferns and gives advice on the care and maintenance of wildlife ponds.

In the fourth of her films about botany, Carol Klein explores the inner workings of leaves - how they harness the sun's energy and turn it into food. Joe Swift meets Griff Rhys Jones for a private tour of his remarkable garden and discovers what a passionate gardener he is.

It's all about the maintenance this week at Longmeadow, as Monty cuts back and divides spring flowering plants. Joe Swift and Adam Frost meet up in Leicestershire to see how they can help a couple of novice gardeners turn a neglected area of their garden into a useable and useful space. Nick Bailey goes to Ham House in Richmond to see how they are coping with the ravages of box tree caterpillar and Arit Anderson visits a garden in Suffolk to find out about the concept of rewilding.
Monty's dividing his Pulmonaria and gives advice on frost-protection, Joe visits a tropical oasis outside Bristol, and Carol looks at Rowans from around the world.

With the arrival of October, it is time to start thinking about getting some onions and garlic in the ground, and Monty Don shares his secrets on how to get a successful crop. Elsewhere, Carol Klein takes first-time gardeners Dan and Dominique for a day out in Devon. They are on the hunt for some seasonal inspiration for their new garden and what better place to look than RHS Rosemoor.

Charge your glasses as Joe Swift visits a 'drinkable' allotment in London where much of the produce is grown to make beer, wine and cider. In the first of a five-part series about botany, Carol Klein looks at the capsules of potential that herald the start and end of most plants' lives: seeds.
Monty is back at Longmeadow, getting stuck into more seasonal tasks. Joe Swift heads to Houghton Lodge Gardens in Hampshire renowned for its walled kitchen garden and heritage fruit collection.

Monty refreshes a container of overgrown herbs, plants alpines and revisits the shrub and perennial cuttings he took a few weeks ago. Arit Anderson meets a designer who is placing sustainability and the environment at the heart of her gardens.

Hugh's new farm is 10 times the size of River Cottage, so he plans to expand production, including setting up a culinary headquarters where he can sell direct to the public; he wonders if he has bitten off more than he can chew.
Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall celebrates the best food that spring and summer have to offer.

Hugh installs beehives at the River Cottage headquarters; the only problem is his fear of being stung; he also takes on his biggest event yet — a wedding party; the newlyweds want their entire menu to only include wild or home-grown cuisine.

River Cottage is celebrating the strawberry in summer with a massive 500-person strawberry fête; in preparation, Hugh and the River Cottage gardeners plant strawberries in every available space.
The day has arrived for Hugh to harvest his honey; with some help from Ken Bishop, they extract 25 lbs.; Hugh then enters some culinary delights into the Melplash Agricultural Show.

Hugh plans a sumptuous menu for a special Autumn feast he plans to throw at the River Cottage that includes a chicken feast, courtesy of Chickenopolis; it is also a good time to go mushroom hunting, but from the air.
Hugh arrives at the gamekeeper's cottage.

Hugh enters his produce into the local Beaminster Summer Show and accepts a jam-making challenge by the Beaminster WI before tracking spider crabs.

Odessa Cotter needs to get to work as a nanny in the home of the affluent Miriam Thompson, but she refuses to take the bus. Odessa is participating in the Montgomery bus boycott, protesting against the inequality between blacks and whites, so Miriam decides to offer Odessa a ride to work every day. Though the community and Miriam's husband insist she not get involved, the relationship between Miriam and Odessa has already changed for the better.

As a mercenary, John Seeger (Steven Seagal) has a reputation that precedes him. That's why he's being blackmailed into performing a risky job: breaking the son of a wealthy arms dealer out of a South African prison. With his friends taken hostage, Seeger agrees to do the deed -- but finds out too late that he's been double-crossed. Not one who likes being taken for a fool, Seeger hatches an elaborate plan to get even that will make the prison break look like capture the flag.

A psychopathic killer is ravaging Memphis, Tenn., by murdering young women, and Detective Jacob Stillwell is on the case. Known as the resident tough cop due to his aggressive tactics, he gets knocked sideways when his girlfriend becomes one of the murder victims. With his partner, Storm Anderson, in tow, Jacob casts the rules aside and infiltrates the seedy criminal underworld of the city looking to avenge his lover's death and put an end to the killings.

Recovering from the psychological effects of witnessing a brutal crime, FBI Agent Jake Malloy (Sylvester Stallone) checks into a rehabilitation clinic for law enforcement officers in the remote wilderness of Wyoming during the dead of winter. He soon finds himself helping other patients as a serial killer begins killing them one by one.

Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.
The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.
The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the north-west in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award-winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking 'Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works night shifts in the NHS, while Ellis' 'Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish 'The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

Three chefs are doing battle to represent Northern Ireland. Tommy Heaney, Head Chef at the Great House Hotel in South Wales, is taken on by Shauna Froydenlund, Chef Patron at Marcus Wareing's two Michelin starred restaurant, and James Devine, the 2017 National Chef of the Year.

After a tense starter course, the chefs return to the kitchen to cook their fish dishes. James is making his elevated take on a fried chicken takeaway as a tribute to the NHS staff who care for his sister. Shauna is also taking inspiration from a personal connection with a tribute to staff from a facility in her hometown of Londonderry. Tommy is hoping to impress with a dish dedicated to the discovery of DNA.

With two courses down it's time for the chefs to cook their main courses. It's the battle of beef with each using the same meat in their innovative creations. Tommy also meets the first baby ever born on the NHS.

It's the dessert course and the final chance for the chefs to impress. After such a tightly fought battle all week, each is hoping to deliver a technically perfect dessert. Tommy and James are both using passion fruit in their complex dishes while Shauna is hoping to use her pastry chef training to score full marks.

The two chefs representing Northern Ireland go head-to-head. Judging as ever are Oliver Peyton, Matthew Fort and Andi Oliver who are joined by Shehan Hettiaratchy, lead trauma surgeon at St Mary's Hospital who helped treat victims of the Grenfell Tower fire.

The winning chefs from all eight regions must battle it out for the honour of a spot on 2018's 'Feast To Say Thank You' banquet menu, celebrating 70 years of the NHS, one of Britain's most prized institutions.

The chefs must prepare fish courses, and after some exceptionally high-scoring dishes in the starter round, everyone is desperate to deliver perfection. Once again, the chefs present their innovative, witty and heart-warming creations.

It's main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. Both chefs and judges alike are amazed at the high standard of cooking and an incredible number of 10s are dished out as the chefs serve up venison, rabbit, duck, beef, lamb and pork for scrutiny.

Werewolves, cat people, body-snatchers and doppelgängers are uniquely queer metaphors; from the classic "The Wolf Man" to queer-authored "Cat People," the monsters of the 1940s express shame and seek to rid themselves of the secret self.

On the journey, Bill picks up runaway Andy Kirby (Andy Shuford), whose Aunt Marian (Nancy Drexel) is Bill's fiancée. Marian's brother asks Bill to lead their posse against cattle thieves and, after a raid proves that Calhoun is involved, Bill agrees. When Bill captures one of Calhoun's henchmen, the outlaw retaliates by kidnapping Andy.

When withered Sheriff Doniphon is overwhelmed by his town's drastic rise in cattle rustling, he calls on his deputy, cowboy Gene Autry, for help. But Autry is bewildered when he discovers that these crafty thieves are utilizing new innovations -- from shortwave radios to airplanes -- to steal herds with lightning speed and stealth. Refusing to be outclassed by modern technology, Autry uses gumption and strategy to bring these crooks to justice.

Gabby Whittaker (George "Gabby" Hayes) runs the Half-a-Chance Ranch for boys from troubled homes. At the boys' graduation, Gabby's friend Roy Rogers (Roy Rogers) performs. Roy later grows concerned when one of the boys, Chip (Tommy Cook), receives a visit from his outlaw father, King Blaine (Lyle Talbot). Chased away by the sheriff, Blaine is shot and killed, leaving Chip a pawn between Blaine's gang and Roy -- who knows Blaine left the take from his last robbery with his son.

Horse trader Roy Rogers has plans to breed his prize mare with legendary stallion Golden Sovereign. Unfortunately, scheming nightclub owner Brett Scoville (Jack Holt) has his eye on the same stud and steals the horse. Sovereign breaks free, however, and mates with Rogers's mare, eventually producing a spirited colt that Rogers names Trigger. When Sovereign is accidentally killed, Rogers is blamed for the crime, and he and Trigger must escape the law and track down the real killer.
A night rider (George "Gabby" Hayes) and his singing partner (Roy Rogers) send Texas carpetbaggers packing.

After the Civil War, cavalryman Capt. Hunt tries to strike peace with Acoma, a Native American chief. However, Judge Wilcox and others provoke Acoma, arresting him and shooting his men, prompting revenge from the chief. In the ensuing battles, one of Acoma's sons is killed, enraging him further. Hunt must save Cherry, a dance hall girl caught up in the commotion, and try to find a way to end the bloody conflict with Acoma.

In the 18th century, American artist Jonathan Adams (Scott Brady) is working in Mohawk territory, where he paints the local scenery. Before long, he meets and falls in love with Native American woman Onida (Rita Gam), but the couple's happiness is interrupted when land tycoon Butler (John Hoyt) deviously pits incoming white settlers against the Mohawk people. Jonathan and his lover are caught in the middle of a violent feud, and the natives become suspicious of the American living among them.

Joining Hayden on his mission is his dim but devoted companion, Dusty (George "Gabby" Hayes). But their plan gets complicated when Hayden meets Fay (Virginia Brown Faire), the lovely daughter of rancher Fred Winters (Lafe McKee). Gentry is after the man's land, and he wants Hayden to kill him to get it.

Undercover government agent Randy Bowers (John Wayne) rides into a small town, happening upon a saloon that's just been shot up. Wary of the newcomer, the sheriff (Earle Dwire) arrests Randy for the murders, but the saloon owner's niece, Sally Rogers (Alberta Vaughn), helps him escape because she knows he didn't do it. Randy then sets out to find the man behind the murders and is led to an evil mastermind named Marvin Black (George Hayes), who has been passing himself off as an innocent mute.

Dare Rudd (John Wayne) and Dinkey (Syd Saylor) are two friends who love to gamble. Dare quickly falls for Tom's girlfriend Judy (Marsha Hunt), who convinces Tom to give Dare a chance to prove himself by running a cattle drive. When he loses the herd in a high-stakes poker game, Dare joins forces with Tom and Dinkey to get the cattle back.

When a bank heist goes wrong, outlaw Yellowleg (Brian Keith) inadvertently kills a 9-year-old boy -- the son of saloon girl Kit Tildon (Maureen O'Hara). Plagued by guilt over the shooting, Yellowleg vows to help her bury the boy beside his father in the now-derelict town of Siringo, Ariz. With criminal cohorts Billy (Steve Cochran) and Turk (Chill Wills), Yellowleg embarks on a dangerous journey into Apache territory to lay the boy in his final resting place.

At a sprawling Texas ranch, a mysterious young man nicknamed Cooncat (John Barrymore Jr.) tells rancher Horse Davis (Basil Ruysdael) an improbable story about a murder at a nearby trading post.
