The story of a middleweight boxer as he rises through ranks to earn his first shot at the middleweight crown. He falls in love with a gorgeous girl from the Bronx. The inability to express his feelings enters into the ring and eventually takes over his life. He eventually is sent into a downward spiral that costs him everything.

In Durham, N.C., the Bulls minor league baseball team has one asset no other can claim: a poetry-loving groupie named Annie Savoy (Susan Sarandon). As the team's season begins, Annie selects brash new recruit Ebby Calvin Laloosh (Tim Robbins), whom she christens "Nuke," to inspire with the religion of baseball. Nuke also receives guidance from veteran player Crash Davis (Kevin Costner), who settles Nuke's erratic pitching and teaches him to follow the catcher's lead.

When car dealer Charlie Babbitt (Tom Cruise) learns that his estranged father has died, he returns home to Cincinnati, where he discovers that he has an autistic older brother named Raymond (Dustin Hoffman) and that his father's $3 million fortune is being left to the mental institution in which Raymond lives. Motivated by his father's money, Charlie checks Raymond out of the facility in order to return with him to Los Angeles. The brothers' cross-country trip ends up changing both their lives.

In a violent, near-apocalyptic Detroit, evil corporation Omni Consumer Products wins a contract from the city government to privatize the police force. To test their crime-eradicating cyborgs, the company leads street cop Alex Murphy (Peter Weller) into an armed confrontation with crime lord Boddicker (Kurtwood Smith) so they can use his body to support their untested RoboCop prototype. But when RoboCop learns of the company's nefarious plans, he turns on his masters.

In a not-too-distant dystopian future, when man's most precious resource -- oil -- has been depleted and the world plunged into war, famine and financial chaos, the last vestiges of the law in Australia attempt to restrain a vicious biker gang. Max (Mel Gibson), an officer with the Main Force Patrol, launches a personal vendetta against the gang when his wife (Joanne Samuel) and son are hunted down and murdered, leaving him with nothing but the instincts for survival and retribution.

Convinced of his irresistible appeal to women, Texas dishwasher Joe Buck (Jon Voight) quits his job and heads for New York City, thinking he'll latch on to some rich dowager. New York, however, is not as hospitable as he imagined, and Joe soon finds himself living in an abandoned building with a Dickensian layabout named Enrico Ratso Rizzo (Dustin Hoffman). The two form a rough alliance, and together they kick-start Joe's hustling career just as Ratso's health begins to deteriorate.

Harvard graduate James Averill (Kris Kristofferson) is the sheriff of prosperous Jackson County, Wyo., when a battle erupts between the area's poverty-stricken immigrants and its wealthy cattle farmers. The politically connected ranch owners fight the immigrants with the help of Nathan D. Champion (Christopher Walken), a mercenary competing with Averill for the love of local madam Ella Watson (Isabelle Huppert). As the struggle escalates, Averill and Champion begin to question their decisions.

Brandt Ruger (Gene Hackman) is a rich cattle rancher. He has a bad relationship with his wife, Melissa (Candice Bergen), whom he treats like a possession. While Brandt is away from home on a hunting trip, Frank Calder (Oliver Reed), a brazen outlaw, kidnaps Melissa and holds her for ransom. Frank, however, treats Melissa better than her own husband does, and before long she begins to develop feelings for him. When Brandt returns, he's enraged and vows to take violent revenge against Frank.

After a bank robbery goes wrong, outlaw Billy Two Hats (Desi Arnaz Jr.) is captured by Sheriff Gifford (Jack Warden). Billy's partner, Arch Deans (Gregory Peck), rescues him, but during the escape Deans gets shot in the leg. The wound leaves Deans unable to ride a horse, but Billy refuses to leave him behind. Instead, he builds a horse-drawn cot for him, and they continue together. The apparatus slows them down, however, making them even more vulnerable to capture from the pursuing sheriff.

Inspired by the Battle of the Little Bighorn, this Western follows a selfish military leader, Gen. Frederick McCabe (Andrew Duggan), who unfeelingly throws his soldiers into dangerous battle situations, and the soldiers who must follow his orders. While waiting to be sent into combat, two of the men -- Harrod (Tom Tryon) and Rogers (Harve Presnell) -- find themselves in the midst of a love triangle as they both pursue the heart of the beautiful Lou Woddard (Senta Berger).

Set during the Civil War, Colonel John Marlowe leads a Union Calvary brigade on a mission behind Confederate lines to destroy enemy railroads and supplies. The colonel is confronted with numerous challenges before reaching Union held Baton Rouge.

Gambler and gunman Bat Masterson (Joel McCrea) rides into Dodge City, Kan., to visit his straight-arrow brother, Ed (Harry Lauter), who is hoping to defeat crooked sheriff Jim Regan (Don Haggerty) in an upcoming election. Bat purchases and renovates a rundown saloon, attracting the notice of Regan's henchmen. A shooting during the saloon's opening-night celebration causes Bat to pursue his own political vendetta against Regan and attempt to clean up the town's corruption once and for all.

Chip (John Dehner), a ranch foreman, approaches aimless hard-drinker Matt Brown (Audie Murphy) in a New Mexico bar. The owner of Chip's ranch has died and left Matt his land, thinking the troubled drifter may be his long-estranged son. Initially, Matt plans on selling the ranch, but then decides to keep it, hoping to impress his ex-lover, Janet (Terry Moore). The ranch, however, turns out to be in foreclosure, forcing Matt and Chip to come up with a plan to pay off their debt to the bank.

An outlaw attempting to go straight while tracking down one of his wife's killers, Jim "Tex" Wall (George Montgomery) finds work on a ranch operated by disabled cattle owner "Bull" Herrick (Bruce Bennett). As Tex begins to fall for Bull's pretty sister, Helen (Sylvia Findley), he also has to face off against two feuding gangs of rustlers, one led by the tough Heesman (Peter Graves). Can Tex escape his shady past and finally end his mission of vengeance?

The four McDade brothers stage a successful heist -- except that three of them are killed. When their wives and mother learn that only one of the young men survived with the loot, they are eager to find out which one. Slick traveler Dan Kehoe catches wind of this strange situation and decides to charm the women in hopes of eventually enjoying the spoils. Before long, however, the lonely females begin competing for Dan, disintegrating into a cut-throat battle royal for his heart.

From worse to terrible -- Civil War veteran Matt Weaver (George Segal) arrives in New Mexico worn down from combat, only to discover his family plot has been requisitioned and sold by cutthroat property developer Sam Brewster. When Weaver attempts to reclaim his land, Brewster hires a reclusive gunman (Yul Brynner) to take him out. However, the gunman proves uncontrollable. He refuses to kill Weaver and instead tries to seduce his wife (Janice Rule), all the while wreaking havoc throughout town.

The residents of a Mexican village are intimidated by deranged rancher Lorca (Emilio Fernández), who assembles 50 gunmen to force the townspeople to construct a church in honor of his dead sons. Vigilante Chico (Julian Mateos), who previously teamed up with six other sharpshooters to protect the villagers in a time of need, learns of Lorca's harassment and decides to round up the old gang members, including Chris (Yul Brynner) and Vin (Robert Fuller), and ride in to save the town again.

When Quintero (Fernando Rey), a Mexican revolutionary leader, is left to rot in jail by the forces of President Diaz, it's up to his subordinate, Max (Reni Santoni), to bust him out. With $600 in hand, he crosses the border into America and hires Chris Adams (George Kennedy), a mercenary of considerable skill, who uses the rest of the cash on more hired guns. After the team is rounded out by experts on close-combat fighting, explosives and knife-throwing, they set off to free Quintero.

Erstwhile gunslinger Chris Adams (Lee Van Cleef) has put his rowdy days behind him, settling down with a wife (Mariette Hartley) and serving as the sheriff of his town in the Arizona territory. So when his old pal Jim Mackay (Ralph Waite) asks for help defending the border town of Magdalena, Mexico, from a marauding bandit named De Toro, Chris refuses. It's only after De Toro's gang kidnaps Chris's wife that he changes his mind, enlisting a cutthroat gang of prisoners to help him.

He suspects corrupt trader Ralph Callendar (Brian Donlevy), but does not have proof yet. Jim's accusations fall on deaf ears with unsympathetic British commander Capt. Swanson (George Sanders). Worse, Callendar, sensing that Jim is on to him, frames the hero for murder.
A Rebel officer (Errol Flynn) and his men use a Yankee bride (Patrice Wymore) to lure Union troops in Indian country.

After serving time for avenging the murder of Cat Dancing, his Native American wife, Jay Grobart (Burt Reynolds), reluctantly takes part in a train robbery in the hopes of using his share of the loot to make a better life for his two children. When his accomplices kidnap society woman Catherine Crocker (Sarah Miles), who is on the run from her violent husband (George Hamilton), Grobart's inner decency protects her from harm as they flee from the bounty hunter (Lee J. Cobb) chasing them.

But things turn sour when her beau, Ben (Reed Howes), becomes jealous. After Mason discovers the men who killed his father, his plan for a duel is sabotaged by Ben, who has been manipulated.

Older lawman Marshal Flagg is struggling to transition from the Old West to the more modernized one -- so much so that Mayor Wilker forces him into retirement. Not one to go away easily, Flagg quickly fixates on his old nemesis, McKay, formerly believed to be dead, who is now back in town and up to no good. But Flagg soon discovers that McKay might be his greatest ally in a fight to prove that the old-timers aren't useless in the New West.

Delong barely escapes with his life. When he tries to alert the authorities, they implicate him in the crime, and he becomes a fugitive.

Dos Papás Pitufo pueden dar el doble de buenos consejos y el doble de amor que uno solo. Sin embargo, después de un tiempo, las cosas se complican en exceso en la aldea. Sobre todo cuando otro accidente hace que Gargamel también se duplique.
Manitas lleva a sus compañeros Pitufos a un viaje salvaje en su caravana hasta Dreamy Steamy Springs.
El auténtico y verdadero Don Pitufo emerge de su libro de cuentos para vivir aventuras en el mundo real.
Patoso y sus desventuras lo llevan a un lugar desconocido. Allí conoce a las duendecillas, unas adorables criaturitas con enemigos que también pretenden meterse con los pitufos.
Pitufo Genio inventa a Pituforobotín, para que ayude a todos los pitufos en sus labores. Pero Filósofo lo reprograma para que abandone la Aldea Pitufo.
A los pitufos les encantan las trufas y las trufas pertenecen a los trolls (ashh). No será fácil que los suspiritos azules tengan un banquete.

Los Pitufos compiten en el concurso de Mr.Pitufo por el honor de ser el acompañante de Pitufina. Gargamel se cuela en el concurso después de encoger su cuerpo con un tinte azul mágico, con la esperanza de capturar a todos los Pitufos.
Todos los pitufos celebran una fiesta en honor a Pitufo Perezoso, y este se ve arrastrado a una absurda discusión sobre pintar los dedos de los pies de Gigantón de un brillante color mandarina.
Mientras los pitufos construyen cápsulas del tiempo para guardar sus talentos, Papá Pitufo está tratando desesperadamente de resolver un acertijo druídico.
Pitufina conoce a una niña en el bosque con la que forma una alianza contra los hombres. En medio del bosque encuentran la casa de una bruja e inmediatamente son capturadas por la dueña.
Los trolls subterráneos utilizan una bola de cristal que permite a los pitufos ver sus mejores deseos para secuestrar a quien la toque.
Los hambrientos Pitufos descubren una cueva llena de comida congelada, y a un ogro congelado que la resguarda.
El hada buena Gunilda le da a Goloso una olla mágica e interminable de avena que Filósofo hace rebosar, vertiendo el contenido en la aldea y el bosque.
Papá Pitufo recuerda las maravillosas aventuras de Soñador en el mar, con tortugas, ballenas e islas desiertas.
Durante una misión para interrumpir la fiesta de Halloween, Gargamel y Hogatha consiguen capturar a Perezoso, quien se ha vuelto rojo por un extraño capricho de la naturaleza.

Pitufo Labrador es el reticente amo de un genio llamado Gourdy, cuyo entusiasmo por ser servicial es quizá algo excesivo. Tras un nuevo incidente provocado por el exceso de celo de Gourdy, Pitufo Labrador le dice algo que no debería haber dicho.
El Pitufo Volador no puede decidir nada, por lo que los demás pitufos lo llevan al bosque para una prueba de supervivencia, donde solo podrá encontrar el camino a casa tomando decisiones.
Papá Pitufo comparte su álbum de fotos.
Práctico se enamora perdidamente de Marina, la sirena que necesita ayuda para salvar a su padre. Pero no podrán continuar juntos.
Pitufo Torpe desentierra una extraña piedra. En ella, puede ver los acontecimientos que van a suceder. No obstante, conocer parte del futuro puede traer mala suerte.
El granjero se encuentra con el genio Gourdy en su jardín, quien causa un desastre, pero de todos modos se le permite quedarse en el pueblo.
Por simple casualidad, un elefante que iba por el bosque se encuentra con Bebé Pitufo, de manera que los pitufos deciden hacer un gran circo.
Cuando el hada de las flores aparece en el pueblo de los pitufos, todos se enamoran de su encanto e inteligencia.

El Pitufo Carpintero se encuentra con una anciana trol en el bosque, quien le suplica que le ayude a librarse de un grano rojo que tiene en la nariz dándole un buen puntapié. Pitufo Carpintero la ayuda sin mucho convencimiento.
Todos los pitufos quieren que Poeta les escriba un poema a cada uno de ellos, pero él se siente superado por la presión y decide huir en busca de inspiración.
Brenda, la pequeña bruja, se siente rechazada: nadie la quiere llevar al Baile de las Escobas de este año. Entonces conoce a Escrupuloso, el aprendiz del malvado mago Gargamel.
Después de que Natural cuida a un pájaro bebé que se ha caído del nido, cree que puede curar a todas las criaturas.
Un pequeño caballo alado pierde una de sus herraduras de oro y Pitufina lo ayuda a buscarla en el arcoíris.

Cada vez que Pitufo Perezoso se queda dormido, tiene la misma pesadilla una y otra vez: se encuentra en poder de Morfeo, un malvado hechicero que quiere capturar a tantas almas dormidas como sea posible.
Debilucho gana fuerza con su propia fuerza de voluntad cuando Papá Pitufo le da mermelada de pitufa para que se la ponga en la nariz, llamándola crema Hazlo todo.
Las aventuras de unas pequeñas criaturas azules que viven en armonía en un bosque, que tendrán que luchar contra los malvados planes de Gargamel.
A Pitufo Filósofo no le gustan los chismes, y crea un hechizo que hace que a todos los soplones les crezca cola. Sin embargo, con cola, los Pitufos son presa fácil de Gargamel.
Fortachón encuentra a un caballero que lo ayuda a combatir a un dragón. Pero el caballero huye y deja a Fortachón defendiendo a los pitufos.
El malvado mago Gargamel intenta cambiar de cuerpo con Papá Pitufo. Sin embargo, algo sale mal y Gargamel intercambia su cuerpo con el perro de los Pitufos.
Brainy se convierte en el rey de la aldea de los pitufos, lo que inmediatamente provoca que las cosas salgan mal.
Newly-weds seek period property in Cumbria for £700,000.
Alistair seeks green Derbyshire retreat balancing rural and village life on £375k.
Jonathan Broom and his wife Deborah put everything on hold while he builds a miniature, Hollywood Hills-style mansion.
A farmer/architect designs a house made up of shipping containers welded together in the shape of a giant cross.
Rebecca and Gregory attempt to transform a single-story bungalow into a cutting edge home in Cornwall.
Jules Hudson helps two retired drama teachers swap busy Sheffield for a new rural life in the Devon countryside.
Nicki Chapman is in Pembrokeshire and has a maximum of £700,000 to help a couple achieve the lifestyle change they've always dreamt of.

Alistair Appleton helps a couple fulfill a childhood dream, swapping the fast lane of London for an artistic life in the Suffolk countryside; armed with £400,000, the duo wants a detached period or ultra-modern home.
Nicki helps a couple find a home in West Sussex that is spacious enough for their six dogs; Nicki visits the Goodwood Estate.
Kevin McCabe, the leading living exponent of cob building, meets a master craftsman whose dream is to build a castle made entirely out of mud.
Michael Butcher and Phil Palmer fall in love with Christmas Farm, near Newbury; they decide to quit their urban media jobs and move to the country.
Rob Hodgson and Kay Ralph plan to build an architectural monument high on a cliff top.
Karen wants to paint her property top to bottom in psychedelic colors.

In Nottingham, twelve Edwardian cottages that started out identical are now anything but; Sarah wants to reintroduce some of the uniformity, but one house insists on going their own way whatever Sarah and the neighbors think.
The team travel to Bedford to help a family of six who are bursting at the seams; they also create an area for the family to eat.
A team of cleaners and DIY experts have just one day to help a household reclaim their space and fall back in love with their home.

Karen Richards of K Interiors explores the use of color; how colorful fabrics are made; Elisha Annandale of Décor Identity shows a home where she uses pops of color; Donald Nxumalo shows an all pink apartment.

Interior designer and decor journalist Kelly Adami shows the best way of adding life to a home with accessories; many designers came together at Design Joburg; Andrew Mackenzie transforms a living space using natural accessories.
South African home design and architecture has truly come into its own; bland imitations making way for modern masterpieces and character-filled design.
South African home design and architecture has truly come into its own; bland imitations have made way for modern masterpieces and character-filled design.
Michael Portillo journeys the country by train.
Deep in the Prairies, Michael learns how communities grew around grain elevators, digs into Indigenous history at an archaeological excavation and learns how to make a Saskatoon berry pie.
Traveling back in time to experience the life of les voyageurs; admiring Edmonton's heritage street cars; discovering how the beaver, once slaughtered for its fur, is now pampered.
Jacqui wants to move back home to Devon after 50 years; Melisa wants to find a bungalow.
Jules Hudson is in South Buckinghamshire, helping a northern couple find a home closer to their family and friends in London.
Peter Maddison visits Chris, who wants to produce a resilient version of his original home, which was destroyed.
Domenic and Sue try to build a tall living space.
Denise Nurse seeks the perfect family home for a family seeking a Suffolk-Essex border home away from the city with £500,000 to spend.

Denise Nurse joins a couple ready to leave their 1930s semi in Surrey and relocate to east Devon; with a budget of £700,000, they are dreaming of a large rural retreat with great views and a large kitchen diner.

Sonali Shah is in rural Devon with a couple who have a £350,000 budget and high hopes of finding a country home that has a workshop for him and an art studio for her; Sonali also meets a family of wheelwrights dedicated to preserving the dying craft.

Sahil Sinha is in love with Isha and wants to marry her. However, his tyrannical father, Jaisingh, insists that he marry the girl he has hand-picked. After a bad argument erupts between them, Jaisingh turns up dead. Sahil, who is viewed as the prime suspect, is arrested and put on trial for murder, and ends up receiving a life sentence in jail. Never ceasing to proclaim his innocence, Sahil manages to escape from prison and goes looking for the real killer.
Abhay and Ritika are forced to enter into an arranged marriage. On their honeymoon to Ooty, the couple tries to make their relationship work despite the awkwardness.
A woman's life becomes chaotic when her lies start to spin out of control.
Subir, a popular singer, encourages his wife Uma to take up a career in singing too. However, their marital bliss shatters when Uma's popularity surpasses his own.
Four sons-in-law marry four brides whose fathers-in-law mistake the men for another man.

Veera, a young bride-to-be, is abducted by a common criminal, Mahabir, and his men a day prior to her wedding. Far from being terrified of her abductor, Veera discovers an adventurous and liberating life.
A good Samaritan always seems to wind up in trouble with the local police.
Sid, a commitment-phobe, agrees to marry his girlfriend, Trisha. However, they face a major hurdle when Trisha's father ends up disliking Sid.

A man is stopped for driving under the influence; a woman claims her husband is drunk and trying to break into the house with a shovel; a deputy is called to assist in a traffic stop involving a possible stolen trailer.
A man has threatened to kill his parents, but when police arrive deputies find an owned and operated drug facility run by the parents.
Two people are discovered sleeping in a car in a high school parking lot; a deputy patrolling Lake Tahoe finds two women who fell out of their kayaks.
A woman says her husband was stabbed by three teenagers; a deputy looks for trespassers at a location where drug users are known to congregate.

The Special Enforcement Detail prepares to take down a person with a felony warrant for theft and drug possession; deputies investigating a disturbance in a field discover minors in possession of drugs and alcohol.
A man with multiple arrests for heroin possession talks about what life on the drug is really like.
An undercover narcotics team goes after a known drug house; a man assaults his own father; a drunk motorist drives over a cliff and into a river.
A domestic violence call leads to a foot chase; a burglary in progress; a deputy finds heroin on a man who was stumbling in the road.
Behind-the-scenes of the planning and execution of a large drug bust.
A bicycle stopped for not having lights leads to the discovery of a stolen 27 foot trailer and its parolee occupants; a brawl in a motel parking lot.
A reported DUI stop yields an intoxicated driver, but her husband leads the viewer into the mind of a drug abuser.
A deputy responds to a 911 call reporting a verbal argument between a man and a woman.
The search of a vehicle reveals drugs and a handgun; a homeless person trashes a woman's house.

A troubled young man with physical limitations decides to fight with the police; the boat patrol on Lake Tahoe responds to an overturned vessel in the water; a vehicle with an out-of-date registration is pulled over.
A dangerous fugitive is wanted for assault and battery; a deputy stops an unregistered vehicle; a look at the daily procedures deputies must follow before going on patrol.
Two children are found riding on the top of a vehicle; a probation search on a lady who has outstanding warrants.
An attempted suicide is reported; an officer responds to an animal abuse call; police do a gang sweep of a residential area in Lake Tahoe.

Detectives and deputies arrest sex traffickers in a prostitution sting operation; a store owner reports a suspicious man looking into car windows; a deputy is called to a business where four people sitting in a car appear to be up to no good.
A deputy responds to a report of domestic abuse along with an assault with a deadly weapon; a traffic stop on a vehicle with an expired registration reveals three women who have some drug habits.

Police execute a search warrant on a marijuana grow operation ran by illegal Mexican nationals; a person reports they found three pipe bombs; in a domestic violence call, a man is reported to be burning all his own property on his front lawn.
Deputy Petersen responds to a 911 call of a girl stabbing another person in a housing complex.
A deputy responds to a 911 call about a possible burglary; deputies answer a domestic violence call, where a man claims his wife choked him.
Police visit a known drug house in Lake Tahoe; a convicted felon has a weapon; a burglar tries to escape in a stolen vehicle.
Deputy Van Buren is flagged down by another motorist that a car tumbled down the side of the hill violently.
Deputies search for four armed men who broke into homes and assaulted and robbed citizens; a deputy checks on the welfare of a woman who had recently given birth.

A deputy finds an overturned vehicle with an intoxicated driver inside; a foreign national from Guatemala is arrested for driving with a suspended license; a traffic stop leads to an arrest on a felony warrant; an intoxicated driver at a gas station.
A sting operation results in the recovery of over 12 ounces of meth; an alarm goes off at a coffee shop; a report of a stolen vehicle at a gas station.
A deputy tries to make contact with a parolee who has a history of fighting; an assault at a gas station; a husband allegedly assaults his wife.
While patrolling an area after a string of recent burglaries, a deputy finds a wanted man; a deputy is alerted to the location of two men with drugs, firing off their guns.
When a forest fire in California forces residents to evacuate, deputies assist by leading people and animals to safety.
A driver runs off after being involved in an accident; patrolling a motel known for high drug activity; a fight breaks out at a gas station.
Deputies investigate a report of a woman throwing objects at passing cars; at a domestic violence call, an intoxicated woman throws heavy objects at her husband.
An illegal marijuana grow operation is found in a mobile home; a deputy responds to a report of a loud and violent neighbor; a home burglary is interrupted by the homeowners.

A car passing through a Lake Tahoe Agriculture check point registers as stolen, resulting in a chase; a vehicle with an expired registration is seen weaving in and out of their lane; a car is pulled over for a defective tail light.
A deputy follows two probationers into a known drug house; a water company worker contacting people about a water issue calls police about an extremely inebriated woman who fell down.
A traffic stop leads to the arrest of a central figure in a major ID theft ring; a deputy answers a domestic violence call; a driver is arrested for warrants after a traffic stop.
Police execute a search for heroin in a filthy house; a report of suspicious activity in a grocery store parking lot; officers investigate an abandoned trailer.
Police attempt to arrest a drug dealer; a young woman is found lying on the side of the road; officers try to catch people who are willing to buy alcohol for minors.

A vehicle fire on a highway; a man claims local citizens have been stealing from his store; Lake Tahoe's SnowGlobe Music Festival; a young woman with a substance abuse problem escapes custody while being treated at a hospital.
An intoxicated man runs through the streets in his underwear; a couple fights in their car; a couple won't stop fighting.
A Special Enforcement Detail executes a plan to catch some burglars who ransacked several homes; a 911 caller reports that a woman broke into her car.
Deputies wishing to be part of the SWAT team face a testing procedure that is harsh and demanding.

Deputies deal with an angry and aggressive transient; a truck is pulled over by a deputy, and one of the occupants is found to have a felony warrant; a man reports that his wife is beating him, and through a hammer at him.
An intoxicated young man exposes the dysfunctional mind of an alcoholic; a known drug user is found roaming a department store parking lot.

Police seek to take down a known drug house where they expect many arrests; deputies investigate a van parked after-hours in a school parking area; knives, bullets and marijuana are found in a suspicious car.
Deputy Jeremy Funk responds to a battery in place and finds a truly out of control dysfunctional family.
The Western El Dorado Narcotics Enforcement team plans and executes the raid of a large drug cartel; the team converges on the operation of a mid-level methamphetamine dealer.
Following a SWAT mission from briefing to execution; a man wanted for assault with a deadly weapon is taken into custody.

A deputy responding to a call in the outlying area of the county finds a large illegal marijuana grow operation; the process of destroying illegal marijuana gardens; an officer investigates several reports of petty theft.
Deputies respond to a parolee who is locked in a residence, and known to have a weapon; a trained dog finds clues that a human would surely miss.
Deputy Lopez responds to a call by a juvenile that his dad is beating up his mom; the dad states: "I have the right to punch my wife."

A woman hides in a store bathroom, claiming there is a man with a gun outside waiting to shoot her; a man is reported to have fallen off a cliff in South Lake Tahoe; two vehicles pulled over for speeding.
An individual is offering Hash Oil in trade to people advertising their goods on Craig's List.

On a trip to the beach, a teenage girl named Tobe meets a charismatic stranger named Harlan, who dresses like a cowboy and claims to be a former ranch hand. The pair feel an instant attraction and begin a relationship, but her father, a lawman, is suspicious of her lover.

Old friends Wallace (Wallace Shawn) and Andre (Andre Gregory) haven't seen each another in five years and agree to meet for dinner. Andre, a once well-known theater director, dropped out of the New York scene to travel the world, while Wallace stuck around, finding only mixed success as a playwright. As they sit down to eat, Andre launches into a series of fantastic stories from his time away, and Wallace can't help but notice how different their worldviews have become.
A mad doctor tries psychoplasmic therapy on a raging woman soon to be a mother.

After James, a blind man, inexplicably regains his vision, he becomes possessed by a drive to make a better life for himself. However, his new improvements -- a nicer home, a higher paying job, tailored suits, luxury car -- leave little room for the people who were part of his old, simpler life. As his relationships buckle under the strain of his snowballing ambition, it becomes uncertain if James can ever return from darkness.
Weary action star Jean-Claude Van Damme (Jean-Claude Van Damme) returns to Belgium to find relief from his troubles but instead stumbles into a bank robbery.
Cardsharp Brady Hawkes searches for his son, who is on the run with outlaws Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.
A fighter vows not to speak until he finds the masked man who killed his father.

While serving in the military, a Marine sergeant (James Marsden) believes his family's ties to organized crime are a thing of the past. However, an act of insubordination and a visit from the F.B.I. send him packing to his South Philadelphia hometown, and he discovers that his brother (Brad Renfro) and his cousin (Giovanni Ribisi) have become entangled with mobsters, leaving him with only one way to save them.

New father Frank (Emilio Estevez) departs for a night out, joining friends Mike (Cuba Gooding Jr.) and Ray (Jeremy Piven) as they head to a boxing match. At the last minute, they are joined by John (Stephen Dorff), Frank's brother. Stuck in gridlock traffic, the guys take a shortcut that gets them lost. In a very dangerous neighborhood, they witness a murder by a gang leader called Fallon (Denis Leary). They flee, but Fallon now wants them hunted down and eliminated.

Called to a French monastery following the appearance of a dead body, Detective Pierre Niemans (Jean Reno) finds himself investigating what appears to be a radical cult killing that's based on obscure passages from the Bible. When fellow detective Reda (Benoît Magimel) shows up, his own murder investigation intertwining with Niemans', it becomes clear that a grand conspiracy is underway, one that spans the globe and reaches all the way back to World War II.

Jonathan Shannon (Ryan Phillippe) gives his 17-year-old daughter Clare (Joey King) an old music box that promises to grant its owner seven wishes. Skeptical at first, Clare becomes seduced by its dark powers when her life starts to radically improve with each wish. Everything seems perfect until she realizes that every wish she makes causes the people who are closest to her to die in violent and elaborate ways.

Secret agent Kristoff (Jean-Claude Van Damme) is assigned to escort Galina Konstantin (Laura Elena Harring), a thief in possession of a deadly virus, on a train journey that unluckily falls on his birthday. Kristoff tells his disappointed wife, son and daughter that he's taking a business trip. They decide to sneak aboard the train as a surprise, only to suspect he's having an affair with the mysterious Galina. To make matters much worse, terrorists hijack the train and go after the virus.
On the Rock of Gibraltar, the team unlocks over thirty years of secrets and lies which help solve two murder mysteries.
Brian Lane knows his days at UCOS are numbered; meanwhile, the team investigate a 16-year-old murder of a young mom by her criminal husband that could be a miscarriage of justice.
As Lane comes to terms with life after UCOS, Esther asks him to help one of her book club friends find her missing brother.
A man thought dead resurfaces as a victim in a devastating fire.
The man convicted of killing Terry Fulton is released from prison to become a murder target.
The suspicious deaths of two brothers might be racially motivated.
Ranjeet finally catches a break when he links the two brothers' deaths to the murder of an elderly Belgian man, but he begins to discover more than he bargained for.
Gerry finds himself investigating the possible murder of the grandson of an old friend.
The team investigate the unsolved killing of a brilliant young doctor.
A dynamic high-flying city lawyer receives a note to say that her terrorist father wasn't accidentally killed by his own bomb in 1982 but was actually murdered by the police.
A distressed dementia patient escapes her care home to report a murder.
Ned and Sasha are forced to work together when the body of a film critic is found in a sewer; it is thought to be linked to the twenty-year-old murder of a concept artist, David Straka.
The team investigates the death of a personal trainer who belonged to a Roman reenactment society.

The arrest of a Turkish barmaid working in London illegally reopens the cold case of a landlord who died in a suspected arson attack on his city pub; Gerry and Steve take a trip out to a vineyard in Kent.
A teenager's DNA provides a partial match with that of a murderer.
Tragedy strikes for Griffin when his friend Ellen Barker is found murdered; the SIO on that case is revealed to be DCI Grace Mackie, a contemporary of Miller's from her training days.
A tape is found containing the voice of a girl who was murdered after it went into a time capsule.
Adam West visits and a race between the Batmobile and Black Beauty ensues; a customer sells the first appearance of Rocket Raccoon.
Artist Neal Adams and writer Denny O'Neil visit the Stash; the guys see a set of 50-year-old Batman night lights.
Butch Patrick (Eddie Munster) stops by the Stash; a never officially released rare Star Wars action figure.
Kevin's assistant, Ashley, learns about comic book retail at the Stash; pro wrestlers want to sell their comic.
Darryl McDaniels of Run-DMC brings his new comic to the Stash; the guys look at a Marvel Silver Age number one issue.
Billy Dee Williams stops by the store to win the Millennium Falcon the same way Lando lost it: a high-stakes card game.
Jason Mewes hangs out and plays clerk at the Stash; Walt wants to acquire a mysterious recreation of comic book art.
The guys attend a KISS concert; Walt lives out his childhood dream of meeting Gene Simmons; Ming considers buying an arcade cabinet.
Peter Mayhew ("Chewbacca") judges a Wookiee contest at the Stash; one of the hottest comic books of the 1990s.
Mike flies in the Batcopter to celebrate fifteen years at the Secret Stash; the guys look at one of the hottest books of the '90s.
Kevin talks comics with actor William Shatner; Walt covets a Mego doll that has unique packaging.
The guys and Bryan visit a "Jaws" museum; super-powered toilet paper comes through.
The guys are prompted to reconsider their preparations for the apocalypse by a zombie comic; an eccentric collector wants Walt's help.
Stan Lee helps a customer who is experiencing a comics crisis; a customer buys a classic issue of Fantastic Four.
Secret Stash employees audition with Walt and Bryan for a role in the claymation film they are making with Brian Quinn.
Comics artist, John Romita, Jr., draws an original piece for the Stash; Bryan shows interest in an Evel Knievel toy from his childhood.
Inspired by an old friend, the guys wear cowboy hats, and celebrate the old Wild West; a customer is searching for an iconic comic from the '80s.
Artist Jim Lee shares tales from the world of comics on the podcast; a comic book brings wedding bells to the Stash.
When Ming gets a selfie stick, he tries to go viral by filming the Stash; Walt examines bootleg toys of an '80s blockbuster.
Jason Mewes brings his infant daughter to the Stash to meet everyone; a customer sells comic book Slurpee cups.
Real-life superhero, Phoenix Jones, visits the store and patrols Red Bank with the guys; Walt reminisces about a Batman playset.
Walt and the boys go on a trip to cross off a bucket-list item; four key Spider-Man issues come to the Stash.
The Stash sponsors a blood drive at the shop with the help of horror queen Elvira; the boys discuss the joys of "Mystery Science Theater 3000."
When a vintage 1980s Pac-Man game lands on the counter, Ming prepares for battle; a rare Beatles board game excites the guys.
KITT from "Knight Rider" pulls up to the Stash; a rare Green Arrow Mego figure and Archie Bunker's grandson.
Lindsay Wagner ("The Bionic Woman") stops in for a Silver Surfer item; Jem and Ghostbusters toys spark another round of banter.
Ming and a customer joust over the price of Batman 111; Wolverine becomes the largest statue to ever enter the Stash.
Kevin and Harley visit for the Yoga Hosers premiere; Ming becomes a lead villain with help from a special-effects makeup legend.
Members of the 501st Legion of Stormtroopers invade the Stash looking for new recruits; the fate of a vintage Ewok playset.
Ralph Macchio seeks a rare "Karate Kid" playset; Ming gets an unforgettable lesson; Walt gets excited about a Mechagodzilla.
The guys prepare for a maritime adventure when the Batboat docks in Red Bank; Batman's first appearance.
Jason Mewes inserts himself into transactions involving a Deadshot statue and a vintage Death Star Space Station.
Actress Katrina Law ("Arrow") wants a copy of Batman 232; old school items involving Popeye, Dynomutt and Pogs.
Walt steps into the ring with a customer over an original Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots game; a rare piece of original Sal Buscema art.
Marky Ramone shares his artwork and bonds with Walt over robots; a King Kong item from 1975.
A Kreskin ESP game reveals Walt's powers of cognition; discussions about Mork from Ork and Dick Tracy's Rogues' Gallery.
Tom Cavanaugh visits the shop; Walt finds a Golden Age classic with "Human Torch No. 2."
Kevin Smith and the guys discuss how "The Walking Dead" started out as a comic book and became a cultural phenomenon.
Legendary horror icon Robert Englund, aka Freddy Krueger, personally delivers a birthday present to Ming.
The Stash & Red Bank cosplayers celebrate the centennial of Jack Kirby; one of the greatest innovators in comic book history.
Influential actor and rapper Method Man talks to the guys about his extensive comic book collection; "Starsky & Hutch" gear takes over The Stash.
Jay & Silent Bob cosplayers take over the streets of Red Bank; the Comic Book Men attempt to make history by setting a Guinness World Record.
Rare and interesting Star Wars items making their way into the Stash; Walt offers up big cash to try and score a beacon for the store.
Kevin Smith and the guys attend the premiere screening of a movie about themselves and the origination of the film "Clerks."
Actor Burt Ward, best known for portraying television's famous Robin the Boy Wonder, reminisces about his time on the set of "Batman" and judges the Stash's canine cosplay contest.
Walt meets his match during a heated negotiation with actor Mike Colter ("Luke Cage"); a "legendary" video game becomes both Walt's trash and Ming's treasure.
Troma Entertainment co-founder Lloyd Kaufman and his crew put the guys through a grueling audition to see if they have what it takes to be in a Troma film.
The boys take a field trip to the Pez Museum to determine if Walt is actually the owner of an extremely rare and valuable piece of Pez history.
When Walt learns that Ming befriended actor Michael Gray ("Shazam!"), he decides that he must meet the "Mighty Mortal."
Kevin and the boys attend the grand opening of Funko's new headquarters, where they get honored with their very own Pop! figures.
Walt challenges the staff to a flea market sales competition.
Kevin rallies the Stash for a game of street hockey; hurricane Mewes blows through the Stash, and no one is safe.
Walt wants the Stash to shoot its first commercial and to have Bryan direct it; one customer brings in a fanboy's dream.
Walt reluctantly lets Ming run a new sales promotion for the Stash based around zombies, but Ming's scary idea might be too frightening for Walt.
Walt and the guys take a road trip to an unexpected convention; the guys find a treasure in the trash; a customer brings in an item Mike wants for himself.

One cook finds themselves swimming against the tide when they have to combine fish with cheese, and it's a rice-off in the finale as the last two cooks draw from their backgrounds in order to pull out the win.
Reality hits when the cooks are asked to create dishes from Hugh Acheson's fridge using miso, whipped herb cheese and celery.

Sketch is visited by John, an extra-terrestrial enthusiast whose tattoo is on another planet, Jay is working on Alec, who made a big mistake with a tiny inking, and Alice is helping out Jenny, whose eye-popping tattoo comes with a shocking story.

The pop-up tattoo parlour receives a visit from Kelly, who needs Sketch's help to remove a lower-back tattoo that's getting in the way of her job. Alice helps out Liam, whose drunken internet shopping led to him having a DIY tattoo disaster.
This episode visits Bonaparte's in Silsden, West Yorkshire. The head chef Tim specialises in "fine dining" and owner Sue Ray assumes he can cook.
The venue for this programme is The Glass House in Ambleside, where Ramsay finds owner Neil Farrell close to tears as another Saturday night turns into a nightmare.
Ramsay meets Francesco Mattioli, the owner of The Walnut Tree Inn in South Wales, who's broke, chef-less and desperate to restore the restaurant's former reputation.
Ramsay visits Moore Place in Esher where joint owners Nick Whitehouse and Richard Hodgson are trying to create a profitable business with a complete lack of know-how in the kitchen.

The venue for this programme is La Lanterna in Letchworth, Hertfordshire. Twenty-eight-year-old owner and head chef Alex offers modern Italian cuisine, a taste of Little Italy in England's first garden city, and the restaurant is run by his best mate maître d' Gavin, helped by his ex-air hostess girlfriend Emily.

The venue for this edition is D-Place in Chelmsford, run by Mexican-born Israel and his English partner Tara. They've sunk £150,000 of their own money into their trendy café bar, which offers a vast selection of fusion cuisine. In charge is executive chef Philippe, producing everything from all-day breakfasts to Hoisin noodles with an astounding lack of flair.

The venue for this edition is Momma Cherri's Soul Food Shack, an intimate 40-seater a stone's throw from Brighton's sea front. Owner Charita Jones produces a menu of irresistibly unique classics from the Deep South.

The venue for the fourth programme is La Riviera, a fine dining restaurant in Inverness. Owned by multi-millionaire Barry Larson and costing £8,000 a week to run, the place boasts top French chef Loïc Lefebvre and an impeccably-trained kitchen staff with Michelin star-studded backgrounds. Loïc is on a mission to bring sophisticated French cooking to the home of haggis, tatties and deep-fried Mars bars.

Clubway 41 in Blackpool is a 40-seater restaurant above a café, both owned and run by David Jackson and his partner Dawn Brindley. Despite being voted Blackpool Tourist Board's Restaurant of the Year, Clubway 41 is in dire straits. David and Dawn are breaking all the cardinal rules for running a successful food business; in fact, there are no rules, and it shows.
This episode's venue is Irish family-run restaurant Oscars in Nantwich, Cheshire, run by Maura - who also heads up the front-of-house team - and her son and head chef Lenin.

The venue for this programme is Sandgate in Kent, where husband and wife team Lois and Peter Hamilton-Slade own and run a small English seaside hotel. They enjoy eating in restaurants and thought it would be fun to own one, so they pooled their life savings with no previous experience in the industry. Here, there's chaos in the kitchen as first-time head chef Stuart struggles with the demands of each menu.

The programme visits La Gondola in Derby, a hotel and restaurant owned and run by businesswoman Daniela Bayfield. In the past La Gondola was the toast of Derby, reaching the height of its reputation in the 1970s and early 1980s, but the glory days are long gone, and La Gondola is sinking fast. The restaurant's decor, staff and food are all stuck in the past.

Gordon Ramsay is sharpening his knives - and his tongue - for another assault on some of the country's scariest restaurant kitchens. Gordon takes on a restaurant abroad. La Parra de Burriana is an ex-pat restaurant in Nerja on Spain's Costa del Sol. Nestling among the cafés lining the seafront offering all-day English breakfast and chips, La Parra is the brainchild of 26-year-old ex-nightclub manager Laurence.

Gordon tackles a pub for the first time, getting to grips with The Fenwick Arms in rural Lancashire. The pub is run by landlord Brian who, after 30 years in the business and a quadruple heart-bypass, still puts in 120 hours a week and insists on laying down the law in the kitchen. Despite their best endeavours Brian and his partner Elaine are £250,000 in debt, and are losing £1,500 a week.

For the last three years Morgan's has been run by antiques dealer-turned-restaurateur Sandy and her daughters Helen and Laura. The beautifully-designed dining room has a prime high street location and should be the perfect eatery for the trendy local clientele, but head chef Phil is grappling with an eclectic menu that includes mashed potato with apricots, and his cooking's just not up to it. Can Gordon help?

For the last 18 months ex Michelin-starred chef Nick has owned and run Rococo, but his past success is now eluding him. The menu is past its sell-by date, the service is stuffy, the food is over-priced and the only thing being fed is his ego. With debts of £100k, Gordon forces him to face his failures, strips down the menu and dismantles the claustrophobic dining room.

Gordon Ramsay is back with his trademark mix of tough talking and inspirational leadership for another foray into some of the country's scariest kitchens. The venue is Ruby Tate's in Brighton, owned and run by ex-actor and failed Hollywood wannabe Allan Love. It's an oyster bar and seafood restaurant, but Allan's never tasted the food because he hates fish. Can Gordon persuade Allan to shape up?

Gordon takes on The Priory, a 100-seater carvery in Haywards Heath, Sussex. It's owned by ex-IT consultant Scott and located in a beautiful former convent, offering bargain roast dinners. Scott bought the place for £300,000, but with an ageing clientele eating for half price, he's losing £5,000 a week. Despite the heavenly location, the food is straight from hell.

Piccolo Teatro is a bijou vegetarian restaurant in Paris run by feisty Scot Rachel. A former waitress at the restaurant, Rachel bought it three years ago and now, along with best friend Stephanie, she's trying to convert the carnivorous French into a nation of veggies. For Gordon, his trip to Piccolo Teatro turns into one of his biggest nightmares yet. Will he be able to perform a miracle, or admit defeat?

The Curry Lounge in Nottingham is a 120-seater Indian restaurant which has been run since January 2007 by ex-sales director Raz, who's new to the business, and it shows. Despite a £500,000 refurbishment and decor like a Bollywood set, the honeymoon period's well and truly over. Enter Gordon, relishing the prospect of tackling an Indian restaurant for the first time.
Gordon heads for Capbreton, a popular coastal town in south-west France, where Tim and Debbie are struggling with their three-year-old restaurant Le Deck.

Henry encuentra a Lydia, pero Beta, la mano derecha de Alpha, lo captura. En Alejandría, Michonne discute con el consejo si deben participar en la feria con el resto de las comunidades.

Daryl, Connie, Henry y Lydia se ocultan en un edificio para tenderle una trampa a Beta. Mientras tanto, el Reino sufre la amenaza de un grupo de extorsionistas que patrulla las carreteras y exige dinero a cambio de transitar por ellas.

Se descubre el espeluznante origen de las misteriosas cicatrices que Michonne y Daryl lucen en la espalda, el motivo por el cual la actitud de Michonne hacia los forasteros cambió tanto desde la desaparición de Rick.
Por primera vez en años, las cuatro comunidades se reúnen durante la feria que organiza el Reino. Alpha aprovecha la ocasión para infiltrarse de incógnito entre los visitantes de la feria.

Se desata una tormenta de nieve terrible que sorprende al grupo de Ezekiel viajando hacia Hilltop. Su única esperanza reside en cruzar la frontera que estableció Alpha y acortar el trayecto a través del territorio que tienen prohibido pisar.

En Oceanside, el grupo continúa entrenando en caso de que los Susurradores regresen. Las tensiones aumentan, mientras los supervivientes tratan de aferrarse a lo que queda en pie de su concepto de civilización.
Se revela el origen de Alpha y Beta. Además, Alpha intenta endurecer a Lydia a medida que se preparan para caminar junto a los muertos, y los Susurradores crean sus hordas.
La creciente amenaza del regreso de los Susurradores dispara la paranoia en Alejandría. Además, Carol lucha contra su sed de venganza.
Los habitantes de Alejandría están paranoicos y enloquecidos con los Susurradores. Además, de regreso en la Colonia Hilltop, un grupo lidia con un inesperado problema de seguridad.
Desaparecen provisiones de Hilltop. Además, un habitante de Alejandría idolatra a Negan. Ezekiel guarda un secreto.
Carol y Daryl emprenden una misión juntos. Mientras tanto, Siddiq intenta resolver un misterio.
Carol provoca que Daryl se sienta absolutamente incómodo. Alpha y Beta tienen dudas sobre una persona.
Una pelea causa tensiones en Oceanside mientras los habitantes de Alejandría se embarcan en una misión de alto riesgo.
El grupo debe averiguar cómo salir de una situación peligrosa.
El grupo debe defender a Alejandría de una fuerza amenazante.

Tras el encuentro de Daryl y Lydia con Alpha, los habitantes de las comunidades enfrentadas a los Susurradores, que se aproximan a la Cumbre, tienen dos opciones: huir o pelear. Entretanto, surgen problemas entre Eugene y Stephanie.

Michonne devuelve a Virgil a la isla misteriosa de la que proviene para que se reencuentre con su familia. A cambio, Virgil promete que le entregará un arsenal que cambiará el rumbo de la guerra contra los Susurradores.

Todos, héroes y villanos, se adaptan a las consecuencias del devastador incendio que destruyó la comunidad. Eugene encabeza a un grupo que parte en busca de Stephanie, guiados por la esperanza de encontrar otra civilización.

Princesa asusta a los caballos de Eugene, Yumiko y Ezequiel, pero les promete otro medio de transporte. Mientras, Beta, en estado de delirio psicótico, guía a la horda de zombis hacia Alejandría para destruirlo todo.

Los seguidores de Beta se acercan a las puertas, y parte del grupo se impregna de sangre de zombi para intentar escapar entre la multitud de caminantes y regresar con ayuda. Sin embargo, los susurradores se mueven con cuchillos entre los zombis.

Fleet-footed Colin Smith (Tom Courtenay) is a rebellious teenager in the poverty-stricken town of Nottingham, in northern England, who enjoys running as an escape from his harsh reality. Caught stealing cash from a bakery, Colin is sent to a reform school where the manipulative governor (Michael Redgrave) promotes sports as rehabilitation by enlisting Colin in a foot race against a prestigious rival school. What the governor doesn't realize is that Colin is not so easily disciplined.

Frank Ross (James Cagney) is an intrepid reporter hot on the trail of a corrupt politician when he is framed for vehicular manslaughter and sent to prison. There he meets the infamous gangster "Hood" Stacey (George Raft), and the two become fast friends when Stacey saves Ross from a deadly knife attack. When Stacey escapes from a courthouse, he promises that he will help clear Ross' name by finding the man who framed him. But can Ross really trust the word of a gangster?

Prize-winning Tennessee marksman Alvin York (Gary Cooper), a recent convert to Christianity, finds himself torn between his non-violent beliefs and his desire to serve his country when recruited to fight in World War I. Kindly Major Buxton (Stanley Ridges) convinces York to engage in battle, where the pacifist's prowess with a rifle earns him honors as he continues to struggle with his decision to kill. Howard Hawks directs this adaptation of the real York's memoirs.

Ex-tennis pro Tony Wendice (Ray Milland) wants to have his wealthy wife, Margot (Grace Kelly), murdered so he can get his hands on her inheritance. When he discovers her affair with Mark Halliday (Robert Cummings), he comes up with the perfect plan to kill her. He blackmails an old acquaintance into carrying out the murder, but the carefully-orchestrated set-up goes awry, and Margot stays alive. Now Wendice must frantically scheme to outwit the police and avoid having his plot detected.

A trumpet player in a radio orchestra (Jack Benny) falls asleep during a commercial and dreams he's the angel Athanael. The beautiful angel Elizabeth (Alexis Smith) delivers Athanael to the head of heaven's orchestra, where he's told to return to earth and blow his trumpet at midnight, thus marking the end of the world. When he fails his assignment, he becomes a fallen angel, and though he's given a second chance, his fellow fallen angels conspire to keep him from completing his mission.

Ivan Igor (Lionel Atwill) is the sculptor at a famous wax museum in London. When his partner, Joe Worth (Edwin Maxwell), burns down the museum for the insurance money, Igor is trapped inside. Years later he re-emerges in New York as the curator of a new wax museum, which boasts incredibly lifelike statues. When model Joan Gale (Monica Bannister) goes missing, however, reporter Florence Dempsey (Glenda Farrell) follows the clues to Igor's museum, where she discovers a terrible secret.

Ralph Willart (Karl Malden) and his wife Annabell (Angela Lansbury) are constantly at odds over what to do with their son, Berry-Berry (Warren Beatty). While Annabell treats him like a saint, Ralph is more keen on his boy's womanizing ways. Berry-Berry's younger brother Clint (Brandon de Wilde) idolizes him despite what his father says, but when Berry-Berry develops a relationship with family friend Echo O'Brien (Eva Marie Saint), Clint discovers just how shallow his older brother is.

Testing his theory that in every man dwells a good and an evil force, the reserved Dr. Jekyll (Fredric March) develops a formula that separates the two, turning him into a violent ruffian named Mr. Hyde. Thinking he has found the answer to one of life's grandest mysteries, Dr. Jekyll soon realizes he is becoming addicted to his darker self as he unleashes his violent side on earthy dance hall girl Ivy (Miriam Hopkins) and fights Hyde to regain control of his body.

Based on the French literary classic, this drama presents author Gustave Flaubert (James Mason) narrating his tale of infidelity and narcissism. After marrying small-town doctor Charles Bovary (Van Heflin), Emma (Jennifer Jones) becomes tired of her limited social status and begins to have affairs, first with the young Leon Dupuis (Christopher Kent) and later with the wealthy Rodolphe Boulanger (Louis Jourdan). Eventually, however, her self-involved behavior catches up with her.

When a newspaper runs a scandalous story about debutante Connie Allenbury (Esther Williams), her powerful broker father threatens the paper's owner, Warren Haggerty (Keenan Wynn), with a massive lawsuit. Warren believes that, if he can prove Connie truly is a home-wrecker, as the article claims, he can file a countersuit against her. Warren then enlists his own fiancée (Lucille Ball) and reporter Bill Chandler (Van Johnson) to take part in a complex plan to turn the tables on the Allenburys.

Novelist Tom Garrett (Dana Andrews) and publisher Austin Spencer (Sidney Blackmer) intend to show how lawyer Roy Thompson (Philip Bourneuf) has been using circumstantial evidence in capital punishment trials. They concoct a scheme in which flimsy evidence will point to Garrett as a murder suspect, but Spencer will exonerate him at the end. Meanwhile, they keep the plan a secret from Spencer's daughter, Susan (Joan Fontaine), who is engaged to Garrett. However, the trial doesn't go as planned.

After Johnny Eager (Robert Taylor) is released from jail, the unreformed gangster fools his parole officer (Henry O'Neill) into believing his ways are changed. In actuality, Eager wants to return to racketeering by opening a dog-racing track, but the man who put him behind bars (Edward Arnold) is in the way. When that man's stepdaughter (Lana Turner) falls for Eager, the crook uses her as leverage to get what he wants. In this world of deceit, Jeff Hartnett (Van Heflin) is Eager's only friend.

Motion pictures may have put Broadway director Chester Kent (James Cagney) out of a job, but he quickly finds a second career producing musical sequences for the movies. Unfortunately, a cutthroat competitor keeps stealing his ideas. That cannot happen on his next commission, a rush job for a big-time theater chain. If his work impresses, it'll lead to an exclusive contract. Chester has only three days, but with the help of his smitten secretary, Nan (Joan Blondell), he just might pull it off.
